papers.abstract: We study the focusing energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation below and at the ground-state energy, focusing on solutions in the upper energy cone, characterized by \[ E(u)\le E(W),\qquad \|\nabla u\|_{L_x^2}>\|\nabla W\|_{L_x^2}, \] where \(W\) is the ground state. Unlike the lower cone, where compactness of critical solutions plays a central role in understanding the dynamics, such compactness is generally unavailable on the upper branch. Consequently, previous results have often required additional assumptions, such as finite mass or finite variance. In this paper, we remove the finite-mass assumption in the radial setting and give a complete characterization of the upper-cone dynamics in the natural energy space \(\dot H^1_{\mathrm{rad}}\), resolving an open problem posed by Duyckaerts and Merle\cite{DM08}. In particular, this establishes finite-time blow-up of the special threshold solution \(W^+\) in the negative time direction in dimensions \(d=3,4\). For non-radial data in dimensions \(d\ge5\), we show that {for solutions in the interior of the upper cone, the limit superior of their $\dot H^1$-norm satisfies an explicit lower bound as time approaches each endpoint of the maximal lifespan,} while forward-global solutions on the upper threshold sheet that remain below this level must coincide with \(W^+\) modulo symmetries. We also obtain a complete classification of upper-threshold dynamics for finite-variance data in all dimensions \(d\ge3\).

papers.title: Ideals in Enveloping Algebras of Loop Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra, and consider the loop algebra $L\mathfrak g = \mathfrak g[s, s^{-1}]$ and the affine Lie algebra $\widehat{\mathfrak g}$, which is an extension of $L\mathfrak g$ by a central element $c$. It is known that the rings $\operatorname{U}(\widehat{\mathfrak g})/(c-λ)$ are simple for any nonzero scalar $λ$. On the other hand, the universal enveloping algebra $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g) \cong \mathrm{U}(\widehat{\mathfrak g})/(c)$ has many two-sided ideals, and in this paper we investigate their structure. We show that the two-sided structure of $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g)$ is both intricate and well-behaved. Specifically, $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g)$ does not satisfy the ascending chain condition on two-sided ideals, but the two-sided ideals still have a nice structure: there is a canonical nested collection of ideals $I_n$, parameterised by positive integers, so that any nonzero two-sided ideal of $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g)$ contains all $I_n$ for $n \gg 0$. The ideals $I_n$ can be thought of as universal annihilators of natural classes of finite-dimensional representations of $L\mathfrak g$. We also study the Poisson structure of the symmetric algebra $\mathrm{S}(L\mathfrak g)$ and give applications to the representation theory of $L\mathfrak g$.

papers.title: Partial Localization and Multifractality in Heterogeneous Population Growth with Resetting
papers.abstract: We study a model of heterogeneous multiplicative growth with mean-field redistribution and independent local stochastic resetting. The model describes populations or wealth distributed over sites with quenched growth-rate heterogeneity, while resets represent random local extinction or bankruptcy events. At large redistribution or resetting rate, we find a delocalized phase and we compute the growth rate as well as the stationary distribution of the population of a given site. We show that reset-free growth episodes generate power-law stationary tails with site-dependent exponents. For weak resetting and redistribution, favorable sites can undergo long reset-free episodes and localize. This produces a partially localized phase, in which a finite fraction of the total population is carried by a small set of sites whose identity changes on an $O(1)$ time scale within a subextensive pool of $N^{u^\star}$ favorable candidates, with $0<u^\star<1$. We derive the corresponding growth rate from a saddle point analysis, and show that the averaged stationary fractions display multifractal behavior.

papers.title: Ekedahl-Oort strata with a superspecial factor in unitary Shimura varieties
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{k}$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>2$ and let $O_K$ be an imaginary quadratic order in which $p$ is inert. For any $a,b\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ not both 0, denote by $M(a,b)$ the unitary Shimura variety that parametrizes principally polarized abelian varieties over $\mathbb{k}$ with an action of signature $(a,b)$ by $O_K$ (subject to certain compatibility conditions). For any $a,b,c,d \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$, there is a natural product map $M(a,b) \times M(c,d) \to M(a+c,b+d)$, which induces a map on Ekedahl-Oort strata. In this paper we focus on product maps where at least one of the factors is superspecial, since most Ekedahl-Oort strata of unitary Shimura varieties contain such a factor. We describe maps with this property completely on the level of Weyl group coset representatives. We also characterize, on the level of Weyl group coset representatives, which Ekedahl-Oort strata of $M(a,b)$ admit a superspecial factor.

papers.title: A non-sober core-compact meet-continuous dcpo
papers.abstract: We construct a meet-continuous dcpo whose Scott space is core-compact but neither sober nor locally compact. The example is a proper sub-dcpo of a locally compact sober complete lattice, and restriction induces an isomorphism between their lattices of Scott-closed sets. It follows that a locally compact sober dcpo need not be determined, among all dcpos, by its Scott-closed-set lattice.

papers.title: Convergence Rates for Lasserre's Upper-Bound Hierarchy on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with Gaussian Measure
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative convergence rates for Lasserre's measure-based upper-bound hierarchy on $\mathbb{R}^d$ using the standard Gaussian measure as the reference measure. For any polynomial $f$ attaining its global infimum $f_{\min}$, we prove that the order-$r$ upper bounds satisfy $$ λ_r-f_{\min}=O\Big(\frac{1}{r}\Big), $$ yielding, to the best of our knowledge, the first explicit convergence rate for this hierarchy on a noncompact domain. We further show that the rate is sharp by proving an $Ω(1/r)$ rate for $f=x^2$, while demonstrating that, without attainment of the infimum, convergence can be arbitrarily slow: for every $m\ge0$, we construct a polynomial whose upper bounds converge at rate $Θ(r^{-1/(m+2)})$.

papers.title: Strongly irreducible operators, $K_0$-groups, and Jones indices in the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the strong irreducibility of a class of operators associated with irrational rotation algebras in the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $\mathcal R$. By developing weighted shift models for their relative commutants, we obtain $K_0$ calculations and splitting criteria for direct sums. In particular, we construct strongly irreducible operators in $\mathcal R$ whose relative commutants have $K_0$-groups isomorphic to $\mathbb Z$ and $\mathbb Z^2$. We realize every Jones index of an irreducible subfactor of $\mathcal R$ as $[\mathcal R:W^*(T)]$ for some strongly irreducible operator $T$ relative to $\mathcal R$. Furthermore, we construct strong generators of $\mathcal R$ and strongly irreducible operators in every type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $\mathcal M$ with separable predual.

papers.title: Existence and classification of solutions for singular 1-Laplacian equations with gradient terms
papers.abstract: We study the existence and qualitative properties of non-negative solutions to singular 1-Laplacian problems of the form \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} -Δ_1 u = g(u)|D u| + h(u)f & \text{in } Ω,\newline u=0 & \text{on } \partialΩ, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary, $0<f\in L^{N,\infty}(Ω)$, and $g,h$ are continuous positive functions that may blow up at the origin. We establish the existence of a positive bounded solution even when $g$ is non-integrable at zero and $h(0)=+\infty$, breaking the non-existence phenomenon appearing in the associated $p$-Laplacian problems. Furthermore, we prove that solutions possess a non-zero boundary trace on a set of positive measure of $\partialΩ$ whenever $g(s)$ grows sufficiently fast near $s=0$; by contrast, when this growth condition fails, solutions vanishing on the boundary may appear. Finally, when $h(0)<+\infty$, we provide a sharp threshold classification of trivial and non-trivial solutions depending on the size of $f$.

papers.title: Loss-independent time-delay estimation via Hong-Ou-Mandel photon bunching detection
papers.abstract: In this work we study the application of two-photon correlated quantum states for high-precision time estimation. To achieve this, photon pairs were fed into a Hong-Ou-Mandel polarization interferometer to generate N00N entangled states with $N = 2$. Two- and four-detector schemes were considered, and the achievable time estimation precision of each was studied, with particular emphasis on the system's Fisher information in each case. Our results reveal that using a four-detector scheme, enabling the measurement of both coincidence and photon-bunching terms, achieves the maximum precision given by the quantum Fisher information, without the need of characterizing system losses. We also show that correlations between repetitions arise due to systematic errors, limiting the precision enhancement that can be obtained by increasing the number of repetitions. Taking these correlations into account, we show that the four-detector scheme outperforms the two-detector scheme in the precision of time-delay estimation. With the experimentally determined calibration uncertainties, the four-detector scheme improves the dispersion by a factor of 2 for the repetitions performed, reaching up to a factor of 4 as both schemes approach their systematic floors.

papers.title: The asymptotic Erd{ő}s--Frankl--Füredi cover-free conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1985, Erd{ő}s, Frankl and F{ü}redi conjectured that the threshold $T(r)$ for the existence of an $r$-cover-free family with more members than points satisfies $T(r)=(1+o(1))r^2$. We confirm this conjecture by proving $T(r)\ge r^2+r+2$ for every $r\ge1$.

papers.title: Schwarz $\mathrm{P}$ and Schwarz $\mathrm{D}$ as free-boundary minimal disks in a tetragonal disphenoid: exact areas
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be the tetragonal disphenoid whose four congruent faces are isosceles triangles with sides $2,\sqrt3,\sqrt3$, so that the dihedral angles are $π/2$ along one opposite pair of edges and $π/3$ along the remaining four. By Smyth's theorem $T$ contains three embedded minimal disks meeting $\partial T$ orthogonally; the symmetry group $D_{2d}$ of $T$ fixes one and interchanges the other two. We identify all three completely. The distinguished disk is a patch of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{P}$ surface}$ and the congruent pair are patches of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{D}$ surface}$, with exact areas \[ \operatorname{Area}(Σ^{*}_{A}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} {K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} = 0.781700961348056\ldots, \] \[ \operatorname{Area}(Σ^{*}_{B}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} {2\,K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} = 0.639630785585503\ldots \] in the normalization $\operatorname{Vol}(T)=2/3$, inradius $r_T=\sqrt2/4$. In particular $2\,\operatorname{Area}(Σ^{*}_{A})\operatorname{Area}(Σ^{*}_{B})=1$, which we show is the Bonnet relation for the adjoint pair $(\mathrm{D},\mathrm{P})$. The proof is a reversal of the usual strategy: rather than uniformizing the Gauss map, we identify Smyth's three Plateau contours as the $\textit{tetrahedral four edges}$ and the $\textit{octahedral four edges}$ --- classically solved by $\mathrm{D}$ and $\mathrm{P}$ respectively --- and then conjugate. Both areas agree with Surface Evolver computations of Ken Brakke to all $15$ reported digits. We also show that all twelve corners of the three disks are midpoints of edges of $T$, each of the six midpoints being used twice, and that $T$ is precisely the alcove of the affine Weyl group $\widetilde{A}_{3}$, confirming a remark of Gandy, Cvijović, et al. (1999).

papers.title: On Stopping Sets and Continuous-Time Decision Trees
papers.abstract: We study stopping sets and continuous-time decision trees (CTDTs) for Poisson point processes. We first give a proof of the spatial Markov property without assuming that the stopping set contains finitely many points or admits a finite approximation. The proof uses the multivariate Mecke formula on the complement of the stopping set. We then prove that every $μ$-continuous CTDT has an explicit exploration representation: between successive discoveries, the explored set grows according to a deterministic rule depending on the points already observed. If $μ$ is diffuse, the points are revealed one by one almost surely; this need not be imposed as a separate assumption. We also allow atoms of $μ$, in which case all points at one location are revealed together. Finally, for diffuse $μ$, we prove that a locally bounded stopping set revealing at most one point is attainable by a $μ$-continuous exploration. More generally, an increasing sequence of locally bounded stopping sets, each revealing at most one additional point, can be attained by a single exploration at successive stopping times.

papers.title: Thermal activation of photon catalysis in difference-intensity Mach-Zehnder interferometry with squeezed thermal light
papers.abstract: Realistic non-Gaussian operations, which can be implemented by mixing a nonclassical Gaussian state with a Fock state at a beam splitter and then heralding on a photon-number-resolving detector, are known to improve phase estimation in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. The existing studies have considered the single-mode squeezed vacuum for difference-intensity and parity detection, and the two-mode squeezed thermal state for parity detection alone as the initial Gaussian resources. However, a real squeezer in the lab actually produces single-mode squeezed thermal light, which has not been studied in a coherent-plus-resource interferometer. We take up this case and using the phase space Wigner picture, we obtain the heralded state produced by photon subtraction, addition and catalysis on a single-mode squeezed thermal resource, and evaluate the corresponding phase sensitivities. Single-photon catalysis, which is useless on squeezed vacuum, becomes a useful operation for any thermal occupation above $\nth\simeq0.2$, and since it heralds with a probability near one-half, it turns out to be the best success-weighted operation over the whole thermal range. In the vacuum limit our results reproduce the known hierarchy, where two-photon catalysis is the best operation. The quantum Fisher information computations confirms that thermal noise enhances the phase information encoded in the catalyzed state, demonstrating that difference-intensity detection closely approaches the ultimate precision bound across most operational regimes, and, together with a loss analysis, verifies the robustness of the effect.

papers.title: Indiscernible Extraction in Theories with Bounded $k$-splitting
papers.abstract: Hanson introduced the class of theories with bounded $k$-splitting, a higher-arity notion of stability, and proved an indiscernible extraction result for those theories assuming the existence of a $k$-ineffable cardinal. In this article, we show that the conclusion of Hanson's theorem is equivalent to the weaker assertion that there exists a weakly compact cardinal, as well as prove additional indiscernible extraction results for these theories in ZFC. Finally, we show that Hanson's construction of total bounded ultraimaginary Morley sequences in theories with bounded $k$-splitting follows from ZFC.

papers.title: On effective equidistribution for product-type self-affine measures
papers.abstract: We establish an effective equidistribution theorem on homogeneous spaces for expanding translates of product-type self-affine measures seen on unipotent orbits along any sequence of diagonal elements drifting away from walls. In particular, we do not require the diagonal elements to lie in a fixed proper and closed subcone. The main new ingredients in the proof of our equidistribution theorem include an adaptation of the methods in \cite{BHZ25} to the setting of product-type self-affine measures, as well as a weighted effective recurrence theorem for intertwined associated random walks. The latter involves decomposing the random walks according to suitable stopping times and applications of intertwined Benoist-Quint height functions.

papers.title: Classification of vanishing fusion rings of rank four
papers.abstract: A fusion ring is said to be vanishing if one of its multiplication matrices has determinant zero. We classify all vanishing fusion rings of rank four. We then provide a more explicit classification in the integral case, which allows us to derive several new consequences: there are infinitely many nonisomorphic simple integral vanishing fusion rings of rank four and no simple integral fusion ring of rank four is either $1$-Frobenius or Burnside.

papers.title: Boundary geometry and concentration points for attractive Bose-Einstein condensates with a ring-shaped potential
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the ground states of attractive Bose-Einstein condensates in a bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb R^2$ under the ring-shaped trapping potential $$ V(x)=(|x|-1)^2. $$ The boundary geometry of $Ω$ may allow the ring $Γ=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:|x|=1\}$ of global minima for $V(x)$ to meet both the interior and the boundary of $Ω$. As the interaction strength approaches the critical value, we prove that if $Γ\cap Ω\not=\emptyset$, the mass of ground states concentrates at a point $x_0\inΓ\cap Ω$ that has maximal distance from $\partialΩ$. Our method relies on exponential upper and lower bounds for the difference between the bounded domain and whole space minimal energies. The essential lower bound follows from a uniform quadratic-growth estimate near the ground state manifold of the whole space problem, which is established by combining the nondegeneracy of the optimizer for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality with a Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction.

papers.title: A Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Time-Modulated Drude--Lorentz Media
papers.abstract: We formulate and analyze a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method for Maxwell's equations coupled to four time-modulated Drude--Lorentz models: modulated in-coupling, modulated polarization density, modulated current density, and modulated effective mass. The use of electric displacement and model-dependent continuous material states gives a common treatment of temporal interfaces while preserving the distinct physical transmission rules. We derive energy and stability estimates, establish spatial and event-aligned time-error bounds, and separate time-integration error from error caused by misplaced switching times. Numerical experiments in three dimensions and in reduced modal systems confirm the predicted spatial, temporal, and switch-timing behavior, including the field-jump effect specific to the polarization-density model.

papers.title: Quantum control of solid state qubits via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: The use of reinforcement learning (RL) in the design of quantum control strategies for pulse level control of NISQ era quantum devices is attracting growing interest. Model-free RL, not requiring preexisting knowledge of the physical system, acts as a black-box optimization tool well suited for noisy devices. In this work, we provide a simulation-based analysis of the performance of model-free RL for state preparation and qubit gate design in a challenging setup: indirect control of NV nuclear spins in a spin-bath. In particular, the spin-bath is modeled via the generalized cluster correlation expansion accounting for magnetic impurities and intra-bath interactions. We analyze the performance of the RL agents by performing simulations with minimally observable environments and noisy, sparse rewards as introduced in (Phys. Rev. X 12, 011059), and compare them to other state-of-the-art black-box optimization tools.

papers.title: Finite Cumulant Towers for Small-System-Noise Expansions in Nonlinear Filtering
papers.abstract: We study asymptotic expansions for nonlinear filtering in the small-system-noise regime. Our main result is that the expansion coefficients of conditional cumulants satisfy a closed finite-dimensional system that can be solved recursively. At each expansion degree, the evolution of a coefficient introduces a coefficient of the next higher cumulant rank, while a high-rank vanishing property terminates this hierarchy, yielding a finite triangular tower. The first layer is the Kalman--Bucy filter, and subsequent layers satisfy linear equations once the lower layers are known. To derive these equations, we establish generalized Zakai and Kushner--Stratonovich equations for observation-dependent random variables and obtain explicit coefficient equations in arbitrary dimension. The conditional cumulant expansion also determines the expansion of the conditional characteristic function. We further obtain an explicit bound on the number of scalar variables in terms of the state dimension and expansion degree. When the observation function vanishes, the construction reduces to ODEs for unconditional cumulant coefficients. Comparisons with existing asymptotic-expansion algorithms illustrate the resulting reduction in the number of ODE variables.

papers.title: Deep Learning of Topological Equivalence Classes
papers.abstract: We demonstrate an application of deep learning to the problem of identifying whether two generating vectors correspond to topologically equivalent finite group actions on Riemann surfaces, showing how architectures developed for semantic understanding have use for pure mathematical problems. In doing so we discuss how desired algebraic structure influences model design, and explore which structural properties of topological equivalence classes the model has successfully learnt.

papers.title: Mixing time of the lazy and simple random walk on a randomly twisted hypercube
papers.abstract: We consider a randomly twisted hypercube on $N$ vertices and study a simple or lazy random walk on this graph. We show that for both walks the mixing time is of order $\log N$, and the model does not exhibit cutoff. We also establish that both walks have cover time of order $N\log N$, and we show that the chromatic number of the graph diverges.

papers.title: Sharp Cramér-type moderate deviation bounds for the self-normalized maximum of partial sums
papers.abstract: Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be i.i.d. random variables with zero mean and variance $σ^2\in(0,\infty)$. In this paper, we establish a sharp Cramér-type moderate deviation for the self-normalized maximum of partial sums under a finite $p$-th absolute moment, $2<p\le3$. In particular, we show that $\mathbb{P}(M_n\ge xV_n)=2(1-Φ(x))\{1+O(1)β_{n,p}(1+x)^p\}$ for $0\le x\leβ_{n,p}^{-1/p}$, where $M_n=\max_{1\le k\le n}\sum_{j=1}^kX_j$, $V_n=(\sum_{j=1}^nX_j^2)^{1/2}$, $β_{n,p}=\mathbb{E}|X_1|^p/(n^{(p-2)/2}σ^p)$, and $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. This proves a conjecture of Shao2010. More precisely, we bound the relative error by the same truncated-moment quantity as for self-normalized sums. The proof compares the maximum with the absolute sum while preserving their common denominator, through a reflected-walk representation and Fourier estimates with distribution-adapted smoothing.

papers.title: Discrete Temporal CSPs et al
papers.abstract: We revisit the complexity classification of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) for first-order reducts of $(\mathbb{Z},<)$, established by Bodirsky, Martin, and Mottet in 2018. Following their approach, we give a self-contained proof of this classification, correcting several errors in the argument. We further show that, with the exception of cases arising from finite-domain CSPs, all tractable cases are solved by a well-known uniform algorithm, eliminating the need for the collection of ad-hoc algorithms used in the original paper. A central component of the proof allows the analysis to be restricted to first-order reducts of $(\mathbb{Z},<)$ that contain the successor relation. We substantially simplify this reduction and generalize the underlying construction. This generalization allows us to apply the same technique to first-order reducts of the triangular lattice graph and of infinite regular trees, yielding a complete complexity classification for these classes of structures, in particular a $\mathsf{P}$ versus $\mathsf{NP}$-complete dichotomy.

papers.title: Why Shallow Neural Networks Learn Sinusoidal Components First: An Orthogonal Polynomial Dynamics Framework
papers.abstract: Neural networks often learn low-frequency components before high-frequency ones --- a phenomenon called spectral bias or termed F-principle. Many numerical studies have demonstrated this phenomenon, and theoretical studies have sought to explain it. However, several goals remain insufficiently addressed: (1) explaining spectral bias asymptotically, including its origin and why the preferred components are generally sinusoidal; (2) extending the explanation to general activation functions, such as sigmoid and ReLU; (3) making weak assumptions about the data distribution; (4) avoiding aliasing effects, such as those arising in finite-domain Fourier analysis; and (5) developing a theoretical framework applicable to arbitrary networks. We address these goals theoretically by analyzing the eigenvalue decay and eigenvector shapes of the dynamics matrix H, which arises when we expand the network output as a general Fourier series (GFS) in an orthogonal polynomial basis and express the gradient-descent dynamics of the GFS coefficients as ordinary differential equations. The graded structure of H enables an intuitive explanation of spectral bias, while orthogonal polynomial theory helps us analyze how learning bias depends on the activation function and, potentially, the network architecture.

papers.title: Singular Yamabe metrics on complements of closed sets
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq3$ and let $Λ\subset \mathbb S^n$ be closed, contain at least two points, and satisfy $\dim_{\mathrm H}Λ<(n-2)/2$. We prove that there exists a complete metric of scalar curvature $n(n-1)$ on $\mathbb S ^n\setminusΛ$, conformal to the round metric.

papers.title: The derived category of a generalized complex torus
papers.abstract: For any translation invariant generalized complex structure J on a torus we construct the derived category D(J) generalizing the derived category of coherent sheaves on a complex torus and the affine/convergent Fukaya category of a symplectic torus. The category is defined in terms of a non-commutative curved deformation of the Dolbeault algebra of a complex torus. We show that this category is independent of the chosen deformation path, which we prove using non-commutative Fourier-Mukai duality. We also prove that the action of O(2n,2n; Z) on the space of generalized complex structures leaves the category D(J) invariant. In particular, T-duality acts trivially on D(J). We construct concrete objects associated to affine Lagrangians in the derived category associated to a symplectic torus and show that their spaces of morphisms are given by Floer cohomology. We show that our construction is consistent with the homological mirror symmetry conjecture (including its non-commutative version).

papers.title: Mod 3 Congruence Families for twisted signatures of string manifolds in dimensions up to twenty-eight
papers.abstract: In the paper, we establish congruences for twisted Dirac indices and signatures on closed string manifolds by specializing the two-parameter modular forms of Liu and Wang to the tangent bundle. Fourier coefficient comparisons yield uniform congruences modulo $3$ in dimensions $4k$, $1\leq k\leq7$. Suitable parameter choices give explicit formulas involving only genuine twisting bundles in dimensions $8,12,16,20,24,$ and $28$, and recover the comparisons of Chen and Han in dimension $24$. The level-one Witten genus further strengthens selected Dirac congruences to moduli $729,27,27,$ and $9$ in dimensions $16,20,24,$ and $28$, respectively. The proofs use Fourier expansions in reduced $K$-theory and integer identities obtained by clearing powers of two from the denominators before reduction modulo $3$. We also construct non-string spin counterexamples in each of the six listed dimensions and identify the additional coefficient that obstructs extending the uniform argument to dimension $32$ without further information.

papers.title: Sharp Hessian integrability for the planar Monge--Ampère equation
papers.abstract: We determine the optimal local integrability of the Hessian for planar convex Alexandrov solutions satisfying $$ λ\,dx\leqμ_u\leqλ^{-1}\,dx, \qquad 0<λ<1. $$ The distributional Hessian satisfies the sharp endpoint estimate $$ D^2u\in L_{\mathrm{loc}}^{P,\infty}, \qquad P=\frac{1+λ}{1-λ}. $$ This settles the weak estimate proposed by De Philippis and Figalli and identifies the larger optimal exponent $P$. We further construct strictly convex $C^1$ solutions for which the distribution function of the Laplacian is comparable to $T^{-P}$ for all sufficiently large $T$. Hence both the exponent and the weak Lorentz endpoint are optimal: $L^{P,\infty}$ cannot be replaced by $L^{P,b}$ for any finite $b>0$. As applications, we obtain sharp estimates in Minty coordinates and optimal quantitative bi-Lipschitz restrictions for gradient maps, including an optimal exceptional-mass bound in quadratic-cost transport.

papers.title: Automorphisms of Free Metabelian Lie Algebras, II
papers.abstract: We show that every automorphism of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ of rank $n\geq 4$ over an arbitrary field $K$ is almost tame; that is, it can be expressed as a product of Chein automorphisms (also called one-row transformations). Moreover, we prove that, for $n\geq 4$, the group $\mathrm{Aut}(M_n)$ of all automorphisms of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ over a field $K$ of characteristic not equal to $3$ is generated by its linear automorphisms, together with a single quadratic and a single cubic automorphism. The same result holds for fields of any characteristic if $n\geq 5$.

papers.title: Postnikov invariants for rational spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper we construct a theory of Postnikov invariants for (complete) homotopy Lie algebras that is preserved by the integration functor of Robert-Nicoud and Vallette. This result is in the same vein as Berglund's theorem, which relates the homology groups underlying a nilpotent homotopy Lie algebra to the homotopy groups of the associated space. We then deduce an integration functor from filtered Chevalley-Eilenberg homology groups to group cohomology groups.

papers.title: On the Sampling of Certain Dirichlet and Prime Sums at Gram Points and their Viscosity
papers.abstract: Consider the Dirichlet polynomial and its prime-indexed sub-sum \[ \begin{array}{ccc} E(t) := \sum_{k\le \left[ \sqrt{ \frac{t}{2π} } \right]} \frac{e^{it\log k}}{\sqrt{k}}, & ; & E_1(t) := \sum_{\substack{p\le \left[ \sqrt{\frac{t}{2π}} \right]\\ p\ {\rm prime}}} \frac{e^{it\log p}}{\sqrt p}. \end{array} \] In this work we investigate the statistical and arithmetic properties of the sets \[ \mathcal{C}_N := \left\{ E(g_n):1\le n\le N \right\}, \qquad \mathcal{P}_N := \left\{ E_1(g_n):1\le n\le N \right\}, \] obtained by sampling these sums at the Gram points \(g_n\) of the Hardy \(Z\)-function. We refer to \(\mathcal{C}_N\) and \(\mathcal{P}_N\) as the full and prime \(N\)-th Gram clouds, respectively. The motivation is that the approximate functional equation expresses both \(Z(g_n)\) and \(Z'(g_n)\) through different projections of the same oscillatory phase configuration, suggesting that the geometry of these sampled sums may retain information about the local behavior of nearby zeros. Numerically, we find that Gram-point sampling produces highly non-generic geometric structures: good and isolated bad Gram points occupy markedly different regions of the clouds, the prime cloud of isolated bad points splits into two anisotropic lobes, and the position along the principal direction of the folded prime cloud is strongly correlated with the viscosity of the Hardy $Z$-function \( μ(g_n)=\left|\frac{Z'(g_n)}{Z(g_n)}\right|, \) with smallest-viscosity points concentrating near distinguished extremal regions of the lobes.

papers.title: A complete classification of perfect state transfer in Grover walks on abelian Cayley graphs
papers.abstract: We completely classify connected Cayley graphs over finite abelian groups that exhibit perfect state transfer in Grover walks. First, we show that a Cayley graph over any finite group exhibiting perfect state transfer has valency $1$, $2$, or $4$. For valency $4$, we prove that an abelian Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(Γ,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if $S=\{a,-a,a+h,-a+h\}$, where $h$ has order $2$, and $4\nmid |Γ|/2$. Combining this characterization with the valency-one and valency-two cases, we explicitly determine all pairs $(Γ,S)$ for which $\operatorname{Cay}(Γ,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer. Our results extend the classification of circulant graphs of valency at most four obtained by Kubota and Yoshino [Circulant graphs with valency up to 4 that admit perfect state transfer in Grover walks, \emph{J. Comb. Theory Ser. A.}, 216 (2025) 106064] to Cayley graphs over arbitrary finite abelian groups and to all valencies.

papers.title: Uniformization of Julia sets of geometrically finite rational maps
papers.abstract: A Schottky set is the complement of a collection of disjoint open disks in the Riemann sphere. We completely characterize geometrically finite rational maps whose Julia sets are quasiconformally equivalent to Schottky sets. We also prove that the closure of the basin of infinity of a geometrically finite unicritical polynomial is quasiconformally equivalent to a Schottky set if and only if either there exists an attracting cycle and all bounded Fatou components have disjoint closures or there exists a parabolic cycle of multiplicity three. An ingredient of the proof is a new dynamical characterization of pairs of arbitrary quasicircles that are quasiconformally equivalent to pairs of tangent circles.

papers.title: Jianmu-Q: Bridging Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Hardware with AI Agents
papers.abstract: Quantum computing offers a promising approach to non-perturbative simulations of quantum field theories, particularly for real-time dynamics and systems affected by the sign problem. Yet translating continuum field theories into quantum computations remains a challenging interdisciplinary task. Here we introduce \texttt{Jianmu-Q}, a multi-agent framework that transforms natural-language descriptions of quantum field theories into quantum simulation workflows. Specialized agents handle theoretical formulation, lattice discretization, qubit mapping, and circuit design, while physical consistency checks and independent numerical calculations provide validation throughout the workflow. We benchmark the framework on three field theories of increasing complexity: the $(1+1)$-dimensional Nambu--Jona-Lasinio and Schwinger models, and a $(2+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory. Across these systems, noiseless quantum-circuit simulations converge toward independent exact-diagonalization and tensor-network results, while selected circuits are executed on IBM quantum hardware, demonstrating an end-to-end, validation-guided approach to quantum simulation of field theories.

papers.title: Cayley graphs of abelian groups, circular colorings and discrete fundamental groups
papers.abstract: For each integer $k \ge 2$, we prove that an abelian group $Γ$ satisfies $\exp(Γ) \in \{1,\dots,k\} \cup \{2,4,\dots,2k\}$ if and only if it admits no non-bipartite Cayley graph whose circular chromatic number is strictly less than $2 + \frac{2}{k-1}$. This refines the algebraic characterization by Krebs and Sankar of abelian groups that admit $3$-chromatic Cayley graphs.

papers.title: ZZ-Free bSWAP Gates under Strong Driving in Far-Detuned Fixed-Frequency Transmons
papers.abstract: Far-detuned frequency allocations in fixed-frequency superconducting processors mitigate spectral crowding but constrain cross-resonance interactions at practical drive amplitudes. Here, we demonstrate that a single strong drive induces a large $XX-YY$ interaction in the far-detuned regime, while a weak second tone tunes the accompanying $ZZ$ phase. The interaction realizes a 150-ns $\sqrt{\mathrm{bSWAP}}$ gate, which can directly prepare a maximally entangled state from the ground state. For the implementations on the same qubit pair at matched drive strengths, cross resonance gives a shorter CNOT operation, while $\sqrt{\mathrm{bSWAP}}$ gives a 33% shorter SWAP operation with a higher IRB fidelity. The multilevel theory further predicts a regime where stronger driving can yield a speed advantage for CNOT as well, a possibility absent in the two-level model. As an application of the $XX-YY$ interaction, we also demonstrate two-spin squeezing beyond the standard quantum limit through two-axis countertwisting. The interaction realized here complements cross resonance and offers a route to efficient gate synthesis and quantum simulation of interacting spin systems.

papers.title: Defense Filters for Robust Learning of Partially Observed Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Robust estimation of unknown system dynamics from partial observations under attack is a core challenge in learning for control, increasingly critical in multi-agent networks subject to adversarial data poisoning. Existing methods either require highly restrictive assumptions on the adversary or yield weak error bounds. In this paper, we consider identifying partially observed linear dynamical systems subject to adversarial attacks with an attack probability $p < 0.5$ at each time. We propose a defense-filtering framework in which a system designer leverages knowledge of the observation matrix to construct a defense filter satisfying full column rank and subspace separability conditions, which enables the evaluation of a single-attack scenario against observed data. Using this framework, we analyze the constrained $\ell_2$-norm estimator and establish finite-sample error bounds for recovering the Markov parameter matrix $G^*$. This is the first approach to provide provable system identification guarantees via a defense filter for partially observed systems subject to harsh attack environments where the attack probability approaches $0.5$.

papers.title: Gromov-Hausdorff Convergence of Constant Scalar Curvature Kähler Metrics near the Canonical Class
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-ample canonical bundle. For any Kähler class $[ω]$, Jian--Shi--Song proved that there exists a unique cscK metric in the class $2πc_1(K_X)+\varepsilon[ω]$ when $\varepsilon \in (0,\varepsilon_0]$, using the properness criterion of Chen--Cheng. We prove that the cscK metrics in $2πc_1(K_X)+\varepsilon[ω]$ converge, as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, in the Gromov--Hausdorff topology to the metric completion of the twisted Kähler-Einstein metric on the canonical model of $X$ as conjectured by Jian--Shi--Song. Based on the technique developed in this paper, we can also give a new proof the theorem of Lee--Tosatti--Zhang on the Gromov-Hausdorff convergence of the normalized Kähler--Ricci flow on $X$.

papers.title: Explicit Ricci-flat metrics on a special Schoen threefold
papers.abstract: We give an explicit convergent representation of the Ricci-flat Kähler metric in a one-parameter family of classes on a fixed special Schoen threefold. The threefold resolves a shifted square-torus quotient with sixteen disjoint elliptic singular curves. Radial Eguchi--Hanson product metrics and fixed flat collars define a positive background with an exact $a^4$ volume defect. Spherical harmonics, tangential Fourier modes, Frobenius recurrences, radial ordered integrals, and the flat quotient heat kernel specify the inverse of the background scalar linearized operator. A boundary transmission series has contraction factor $1/15$. Independent weighted zeroth-order and six-dimensional Schauder estimates give the inverse bound needed for the quadratic and cubic Monge--Ampère terms. The resulting source-degree recursion converges for $0<a\le2^{-2260}$, with explicit coefficient, potential-tail, and relative metric-tail bounds. The representation uses specified kernels, prescribed integrals, and convergent series; its parameter interval is a sufficient quantitative bound on this fixed model.

papers.title: Operator space theory from the maximal viewpoint
papers.abstract: We initiate a theory of ``operator spaces" (in other words subspaces of $C^*$-algebras) with an emphasis on the maximal tensor product. The natural morphisms become the maximally bounded maps instead of the completely bounded ones. With this new looking glass we first examine various issues : lifting and extension properties, local reflexivity, inner derivations, similarity problems.This first part is semi-expository while the second one focuses on the class of von Neumann algebras $M$ such that any completely bounded unital homomorphism on a $C^*$-algebra with values in $M$ is maximally bounded (or equivalently is similar to a $*$-homomorphism via a similarity belonging to $M$). We show that this holds if and only if $M$ is the direct sum of a finite von Neumann algebra and an injective one. This also characterizes the $M$'s such that all completely bounded derivations into $M$ are inner. Our main tool for this is a new characterization of injective von Neumann algebras.

papers.title: Synergistic charging of a quantum battery via Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and non-Markovian noise
papers.abstract: Protecting quantum batteries from environmental noise remains a challenge. Using exact Burshtein-Kubo equations, we study a two-spin quantum battery with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) coupling under indepen dent local longitudinal random telegraph noise (RTN). At a fixed effective noise scale, the DM-assisted slow switching protocol yields a superadditive transient ergotropy gain and near-maximal ergotropy during the initial charging stage, while the no-DM slow-switching control reaches comparable ergotropy only in a later revival. A finite superadditive region persists at fixed RTN amplitude, with protocol-dependent location and gain. In the Ising model, the enhancement is nonmonotonic in DM strength, with intermediate coupling giving near-optimal performance. Dressed-channel analysis associates this enhancement with changes in transition frequencies and longitudinal-noise matrix elements that reduce slow-RTN spectral weight. Superadditivity also persists in the tested anisotropic XY model.

papers.title: On the exact quantization of BCOV Theory on Calabi-Yau Manifolds
papers.abstract: We announce the solution of constructing perturbative quantum BCOV invariants on arbitrary Calabi-Yau manifolds. In this note, we outline the construction and present an explicit solution. The quantization includes all descendant fields and all loop orders, and expresses the quantum BCOV interaction by an explicit integration over the moduli space of marked Riemann surfaces. This canonical solution provides a mathematical construction of all higher genus BCOV invariants on compact Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are conjecturally equivalent to all higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants on the mirror.

papers.title: An introduction to algebraic groups
papers.abstract: We review the theory of abelian varieties and, more generally, algebraic groups, with a view toward arithmetic applications. We discuss their models over the rings of integers of number fields, their reductions modulo primes, their torsion points (together with their natural Galois action), and the interplay of these notions through characteristic polynomials of Frobenius.

papers.title: Opinion bubbles in the quantum Buridan's ass problem
papers.abstract: The quantum Buridan's ass problem concerns a network of interconnected nodes in which transitions between the nodes are governed by the laws of quantum mechanics. In such situations interference between probability amplitudes plays a key role in determining whether the probability of leaving the initial node is large or small and also the speed at which the associated transitions occur. In this paper we extend this idea to consider transitions between one given set of coupled nodes and the remainder of the network. We have in mind a quantum analogy to changing an opinion, in which the initially occupied set of nodes is one opinion bubble, with the remaining parts of the network corresponding to a different opinion. We find that quantum interference again plays a crucial role in the dynamics. A further key component is the role of symmetry between the nodes and their interconnections, as it is symmetry that lies at the heart of the Buridan's ass puzzle. In the classical Buridan's ass paradox it is symmetry between competing alternatives that freezes the ass into indecision. In the quantum case, however, interference results in a far richer dynamics.

papers.title: On a conjecture of King-Tollu-Toumazet for rectangular Kostka coefficients
papers.abstract: A conjecture of King, Tollu and Toumazet predicts the behavior of small Littlewood--Richardson coefficients under stretching: if $c^ν_{λ,μ}=3$, then $c^{Mν}_{Mλ,Mμ}$ equals $2M+1$ or $\binom{M+2}{2}$ for every positive integers $M$. This corresponds to the Hilbert functions of a conic, or of the projective plane. We prove their conjecture for all rectangular Kostka coefficients $K_{λ,\mathbf{a}}$. We realize them as the weight multiplicities of the homogeneous coordinate ring of the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(k,n)$, or equivalently the weight spaces of semi-invariants of the $n$-subspace quiver with dimension vector $β=(k,1,1,\dotsc,1)$. For a weight $σ$, we show that if $β$ is $σ$-stable, then the dimension of the corresponding weight space is at least $n-2$ when $k=2$ and at least $4$ for every Grassmannian other than $\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)$, $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ and $\mathrm{Gr}(3,5)$. These three cases are precisely when the associated moduli space of $σ$-stable representations has dimension at most two. Via $σ$-stable decomposition, the two alternatives are determined as follows: $2M+1$ for $\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)$, and $\binom{M+2}{2}$ for $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ and $\mathrm{Gr}(3,5)$.

papers.title: A variation on local trilinear form
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a $p$-adic field and $M$ the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2^3(F)$ consisting of triples with equal determinants. For each unitary principal series $L$-packet of $M$ whose central character is trivial on the diagonal $F^\times$, we determine its unique member distinguished by the diagonal $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$.

papers.title: Looking Beyond Visibility: Resolving the Temporal Structure of Continuous-Wave Four-Photon Hong-Ou-Mandel Interference
papers.abstract: Hong-Ou-Mandel interference underpins many photonic quantum information protocols and is commonly characterized by a single visibility parameter. This quantity is typically obtained by averaging over a fixed coincidence window, thereby discarding details of the underlying temporal structure that are critical in continuous-wave processes. Four-photon interference with continuous-wave sources furthermore requires photon pairs with long coherence times, which we generate in microring resonators and measure with ultrafast time-resolved detection. Here, we model and resolve their interference and temporal structure by recording all four photon arrival times and mapping their relative delays onto a three-dimensional coincidence histogram relative to a trigger detection. The resulting structure preserves relative arrival-time correlations that are usually discarded and enables post-processed optimization of coincidence windows to trade off visibility against count rate. This method provides a general benchmark for continuous-wave sources in interference-based quantum network protocols.

papers.title: The Tilted Sampling Problem: Optimism, Posterior Sampling, and Logarithmic Regret
papers.abstract: Many modern learning systems are used not to select a single best action, but to sample diverse high-quality outputs. Examples include entropy-regularized reinforcement learning, RLHF, and reward-guided generative modeling. Motivated by these settings, we study tilted sampling: an online learning problem in which the goal is to sample from the Gibbs distribution induced by an unknown reward function. We define sampling regret as the temperature-normalized cumulative KL divergence between the learner's distribution and the Gibbs target, corresponding to the suboptimality gap in entropy-regularized reward maximization. Our framework generalizes recent sampling-based and KL-regularized formulations in bandits and reinforcement learning. Our main contribution is a general regret framework that captures the different uncertainty structure of tilted sampling and classical regret minimization. While standard regret scales as $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ due to first-order uncertainty, sampling regret is governed by squared confidence widths, yielding logarithmic-in-$T$ regret in standard settings at fixed temperature. We develop sampling analogues of UCB and Thompson sampling (UCS and TS$^2$) and provide unified regret decompositions that explain and extend recent logarithmic guarantees, including the first Bayesian sampling-regret decomposition based on new bounds for posterior-random Gibbs distributions. Our results show that learning to sample from a soft-optimal distribution is statistically distinct from learning to identify a hard optimum.

papers.title: Reconstruction of Fano manifolds from the orthogonal to an exceptional vector bundle
papers.abstract: Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth complex Fano manifolds of dimension at least three with very ample anticanonical bundles and let $V_X$ and $V_Y$ be exceptional vector bundles on $X$ and $Y$, respectively. We prove that a Fourier--Mukai equivalence $V_X^\perp\simeq V_Y^\perp$ implies $X\simeq Y$.

papers.title: Local Convexity and Planarity Estimates for Mean Curvature Flow
papers.abstract: We establish local convexity and cylindrical pinching estimates for hypersurface mean curvature flow under an intermediate convexity condition and integral bounds on the mean curvature. These estimates hold after a positive waiting time and do not require pointwise upper bounds for the mean curvature on the parabolic boundary. In arbitrary codimension, we also establish local planarity estimates for properly defined flows satisfying a uniform $c_n$-pinching condition, without assuming bounded curvature. As applications, the hypersurface estimates yield convexity and cylindrical pinching for complete, spacetime-proper ancient hypersurface flows with uniform Euclidean area growth, without any bounded-curvature assumption. The planarity estimates imply that every complete, connected, spacetime-proper ancient flow satisfying the uniform $c_n$-pinching condition is either a static affine $n$-plane or lies in a fixed affine $(n+1)$-plane for all time.

papers.title: Isaac's Condition (TU) is false
papers.abstract: In 2006 Isaac reduced the simple normality to base $2$ of $\sqrt s$, for $s$ not a perfect square, to a property of dyadic expansions that he called Condition~(TU): the upper frequency of the digit~$1$ in $\sqrtν$, along any subsequence, depends only on the tail of the expansion of $ν$. We show that Condition~(TU) is false, already for the full sequence. We give two proofs. The first is elementary and turns Isaac's own reduction against the condition. The second uses the theorem of Kaufman and Mosquera--Shmerkin on the Fourier decay of smooth images of self-similar measures, and gives counterexamples for almost every point of a Cantor measure. All results are machine-verified in Lean~4; the second proof uses the two cited theorems as hypotheses.

papers.title: Cutoff Phenomenon for the Glauber-Misanthrope process in a perturbative regime
papers.abstract: We investigate the Glauber--Misanthrope process, obtained by superposing a Misanthrope dynamics with finite site capacity and a Glauber dynamics which creates or annihilates particles one at a time at each site. In a perturbative regime around the diffusively scaled partial exclusion process, we prove the cutoff phenomenon and identify the limiting mixing time. Our approach relies on the information percolation framework developed by Lubetzky and Sly and extended by Tran, which we adapt to accommodate multiple occupancy per site and account for the two distinct correlation mechanisms generated by the Misanthrope and Glauber dynamics. Our lower bound on the mixing time holds under assumptions more general than those required for the matching upper bound.

papers.title: A family of algebras that connects positroids, the Theta conjecture, the Delta conjecture, and Eulerian quasisymmetric functions
papers.abstract: We define a family of algebras $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,a,b}$ whose Hilbert series, when $n\le a+b\le n+2$, $a>0$, and $0<b<n$, enumerate certain positroid cells by codimension. Equivalently, these series enumerate certain affine permutations by length. We determine the graded $\mathfrak{S}_n$-module structure of these algebras by using exact sequences to derive an invertible recursion for their graded Frobenius characteristics when $a+b\ge n$ and then passing to the limit $a\rightarrow\infty$. In particular, the graded Frobenius characteristic $\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b-1}]/I_{a+b-1,a,b};q)=\operatorname{rev}_q(ω((Θ_{e_{a-1}}Θ_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $\operatorname{rev}_q$ reverses the $q$-coefficients and the specialization $(Θ_{e_{a-1}}Θ_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}$ appears in the Theta conjecture. For $a,b\ge1$, we also show that $e_a^\perp\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b}]/I_{a+b,a,b};q)=q^{\binom{a}{2}}\operatorname{rev}_q(ω((Δ_{e_{a-1}}^\prime e_b)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $Δ_{e_{k-1}}^\prime e_n$ occurs in the Delta conjecture. In the three cases $a+b-n=0,1,2$, the ungraded Frobenius characteristics agree with three families of Eulerian quasisymmetric functions, respectively. We also construct an open subvariety of $(\mathbb{P}^{k-1})^n$ whose rational Chow ring is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k}$. This variety admits a stratification induced by certain positroids. Its strata need not be affine, and their codimension generating function equals $\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k};q)$.

papers.title: GPU Parallel Pareto Local Search for Multi-objective QUBO
papers.abstract: We revisit Pareto Local Search (PLS) for multi-objective quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems. Multi-objective QUBO formulations have gained increasing attention as a universal modeling method and natural input for quantum optimization. While exact methods exist, their unconstrained binary structure makes them well-suited for heuristics such as PLS. At the same time, GPUs offer a powerful classical alternative to quantum-inspired optimization. We develop an efficient GPU-based parallel implementation of PLS for multi-objective QUBO problems. Our approach combines coarse-grained and fine-grained parallelization. On the coarse-grained level, an initial set of supported solutions is generated using weighted-sum optimization, from which multiple PLS processes are started in parallel. At the fine-grained level, neighborhood exploration is parallelized on the GPU by simultaneously evaluating binary-flip candidate solutions across all objectives. Non-dominated solutions are maintained using an ND-Tree data structure to support efficient Pareto updates. The implementation combines several known PLS techniques within a unified CPU/GPU hybrid architecture. We describe the algorithmic components, the GPU-specific design decisions, and report results from a computational study evaluating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Tauberian rates and the Baire property of ideals
papers.abstract: We study Tauberian conditions on the successive differences of real sequences which ensure that: (i) ordinary convergence coincides with ideal convergence; or (ii) every ordinary accumulation point is an ideal cluster point; or (iii) every ordinary accumulation point is an ideal limit point. First, we prove that an ideal $\mathcal{I}$ has the Baire property if and only if there exists a positive sequence $(r_n)$ tending to zero, with $\sum_n r_n=\infty$, such that $$ |x_{n+1}-x_n|=O(r_n) $$ is a Tauberian condition for any of the three previous statements. Second, for analytic $P$-ideals, we characterize the validity of the Tauberian rate $O(1/n)$ in terms of properties of lower semicontinuous submeasures which represent it. Lastly, in the case of statistical limit points, we prove that $o(1/n)$ is a Tauberian condition for the statement (iii), whereas $O(1/n)$ need not suffice: in this sense, $o(1/n)$ is an optimal Tauberian rate for (iii). On the other hand, for statistical cluster points in (ii), $O(1/n)$ is an optimal one among nonincreasing rates. For every positive null sequence $(r_n)$ with divergent sum, we also construct a summable ideal $\mathcal{I}$ for which $o(r_n)$ is an optimal Tauberian rate for both statements (ii) and (iii).

papers.title: Cohomogeneity one Hermann actions and backward mean curvature flows
papers.abstract: Principal orbits of cohomogeneity one Hermann actions form a natural class of equifocal hypersurfaces in symmetric spaces of compact type. Based on Kollross's classification of cohomogeneity one actions on irreducible symmetric spaces of compact type, we obtain the time evolution of the squared norm of the shape operator and the mean curvature along the long-time solution of the backward mean curvature flows starting from their principal orbits. These results explicitly describe the authors' previous generalization of the results of Liu-Terng on backward mean curvature flows of isoparametric hypersurfaces to this class of equifocal hypersurfaces.

papers.title: Scalar curvature, volume, and Weil-Petersson translation length
papers.abstract: We construct metrics on pseudoAnosov mapping tori that make every fiber an intrinsically hyperbolic stable minimal surface, and which have scalar curvature identically -6. Using this, we give a new proof (with improved constant) of an inequality bounding the hyperbolic volume of a pseudoAnosov mapping torus by the Weil-Petersson translation length (and consequently, the entropy) of its monodromy.

papers.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Optimization for Emergency-Priority Traffic Signal Control
papers.abstract: Emergency-priority traffic signal control requires reducing emergency-vehicle delay while limiting disruption to ordinary traffic. This work investigates a finite-horizon QUBO formulation and compares Exact QUBO optimization, QAOA, CVaR-QAOA, a quantum machine-learning policy, fixed-time control, and max-pressure control in a three-intersection corridor. The study evaluates three traffic-demand regimes, examines the effect of the emergency-priority weight, and compares quantum solutions with the exact QUBO optimum. The optimization-based controllers achieved reliable emergency progression across all tested demand regimes, while max-pressure produced lower ordinary-traffic delay. Increasing emergency priority reduced emergency travel time but increased congestion, with diminishing improvements at larger weights. CVaR-QAOA reproduced the exact QUBO solution more accurately than standard QAOA, although the resulting differences in closed-loop traffic performance were comparatively small.

papers.title: Strong NP-Hardness of Rank-2 Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
papers.abstract: Nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) approximates a nonnegative matrix by the product of two nonnegative matrices with a prescribed inner dimension~$r$. The existence of an exact NMF can be decided in polynomial time for every fixed~$r$, and a best rank-$1$ NMF in the Frobenius norm can be obtained from a truncated singular value decomposition. We prove that computing a best rank-$2$ NMF in the Frobenius norm is strongly NP-hard. Our proof uses a polynomial-time reduction from \textsc{Clique} that produces symmetric positive-definite, completely positive matrices with polynomially bounded integer entries. The same reduction also establishes strong NP-hardness of rank-$2$ symmetric NMF.

papers.title: Volterra operators on the BMOA space of Dirichlet series
papers.abstract: In this paper, we completely characterize the boundedness and compactness of Volterra operators on \(BMOA_{\mathcal D}\), the BMOA space of Dirichlet series, and estimate their essential and weak essential norms. We further prove that compactness, weak compactness, and complete continuity are equivalent for these operators. In particular, every Dirichlet polynomial symbol induces a compact Volterra operator on \(BMOA_{\mathcal D}\). We also prove that every such symbol induces a compact Volterra operator on the Bergman space of Dirichlet series \(\mathcal A_μ^1\) for every admissible measure \(μ\), extending the corresponding compactness theorem, previously established for \(1<p<\infty\), to the endpoint \(p=1\).

papers.title: On Minimum Divergence for Distribution Reconstruction
papers.abstract: We study the possibility of generalizing maximum-entropy reconstruction, which approximately recovers a probability distribution from finitely many (generalized) moments by minimizing the Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence to a reference measure. The reconstruction lies in an exponential family and is also the best KL approximation of the unknown distribution within that family: moment matching and information projection coincide. Replacing KL by a smooth f-divergence, the reconstruction still exists in an associated family, but the best approximation property does not. Specifically, a family is called entropy-adapted if the projection of any distribution matches its moments. We show that, up to equivalence, KL is the only $C^2$ f-divergence that is entropy-adapted, whatever the choice of the generalized moments. We illustrate the consequences of this failure numerically.

papers.title: Twisted Artin-Schreier Theory I: $(C_p \rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of local function fields
papers.abstract: Over any field $K$ of characteristic $p$, we parametrize the $(C_p\rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of $K$ using pairs of elements $(g,a) \in K\times K^\times$, via a "twisted" variant of Artin-Schreier theory. Focusing on the case of the local function field $K := \mathbb F_q(\!(π)\!)$ over a finite field $\mathbb F_q$ of characteristic $p$, we use this parametrization to obtain an exact formula for the count of all $(C_p\rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of $K$ with a given discriminant.

papers.title: Provably Efficient Risk-Sensitive Offline Reinforcement Learning via Optimized Certainty Equivalents
papers.abstract: Risk-sensitive reinforcement learning (RL) addresses decision-making under uncertainty and adverse outcomes. Learning risk-sensitive policies from fixed datasets is important when additional interaction with the environment is costly. Existing work on risk-sensitive RL focuses on online settings or specific risk measures, leaving a general theoretical understanding of its offline setting underdeveloped. In this work, we investigate efficient offline risk-sensitive RL using the optimized certainty equivalent (OCE), a general class of risk measures. We consider two formulations: dynamic-OCE RL, which applies OCE recursively at each step, and static-OCE RL, which applies a single OCE to the cumulative rewards. Under the tabular setting, we develop pessimistic value-iteration algorithms for both formulations and establish tight sublinear suboptimality bounds, explicitly capturing how risk sensitivity, encoded by utility functions, affects learning difficulty. Moreover, we establish minimax suboptimality lower bounds to characterize the problem's fundamental limits. To handle large state spaces, we further develop pessimistic least-squares value-iteration algorithms that incorporate the general OCE risk criterion into linear function approximation. We establish utility-dependent sublinear guarantees with explicit dependence on the feature dimension $d$. To our knowledge, we provide the first offline algorithms along with the first upper and lower suboptimality bounds for both dynamic- and static-OCE RL.

papers.title: Rich-neighbor 5-edge-colorings of subcubic graphs whose 3-vertices induce a matching
papers.abstract: Let $\varphi$ be a proper edge-coloring of a graph $G$. An edge is called rich if all edges adjacent to it receive pairwise distinct colors. The coloring $\varphi$ is a rich-neighbor edge-coloring if every non-isolated edge is adjacent to a rich edge. Petruševski and Škrekovski introduced this notion as a relaxation of strong edge-coloring and conjectured that every connected subcubic graph other than $K_4$ admits a rich-neighbor $5$-edge-coloring. We establish the conjectured bound for every subcubic graph $G$ satisfying $Δ(G[V_3])\leq 1,$ where $V_3$ is the set of vertices of degree $3$ in $G$. Equivalently, the $3$-vertices of $G$ induce a matching together with isolated vertices. This extends the result of Chen, Tan and Zhou for subcubic graphs with no adjacent $3$-vertices.

papers.title: Edge ideals of gapfree graphs with matching number $3$
papers.abstract: We prove that if $G$ is a gapfree graph with matching number $3$, then every power $I(G)^q$, $q\geq2$, of its edge ideal has linear quotients, and hence a linear resolution. Our approach combines graph reductions based on clique domination of gapfree graphs and matching number with operations preserving linear quotients. We reduce the problem to $26$ non-co-chordal graphs on at most seven vertices. A new preservation theorem for gapfree edge addition, together with known results on duplication and gapfree expansion, handles all but one of these graphs. For the remaining graph on seven vertices, we construct a linear quotients ordering for the square and extend it recursively to every higher power.

papers.title: Localisation of the monkey walk with an "impurity" at the origin
papers.abstract: The monkey walk is a model of reinforced random walk introduced by Boyer and Solis-Salas as a model for the exploratory behaviour of capuchin monkeys. At each step of the walk, the walker flips a biased coin to determine whether to take a simple, symmetric random walk step on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ or to "relocate", i.e. choose a time uniformly at random in its past and jump to where it was at that time. More recently, Boyer, Falcón-Cortés, Giuggioli and Majumdar looked at a modification of the model, where the probability to relocate is $ξ_0$ when the walker sits at the origin and $ξ>ξ_0$ anywhere else. We prove that, for all $ξ_0\in (0,1)$, if $ξ$ is sufficiently close to 1, then the monkey walk "localises", i.e. the position of the walker at time $n$, $W_n$, converges in distribution without any renormalisation. (We in fact prove convergence of the occupation measure of the walker.) This is in contrast with the case when $ξ= ξ_0$, for which it is known that $W_n/\sqrt{\log n}$ converges in distribution to a standard Gaussian (we say that the walk "diffuses"). Our proof relies on seeing the monkey walk as an infinitely-many colour Pólya urn (a.k.a. measure-valued Pólya process - MVPP) and then prove convergence of this urn, which is not straightforward as theorems from the literature on MVPPs do not apply directly.

papers.title: Weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}$-object
papers.abstract: $\mathbb{P}$-objects were introduced by Huybrechts and Thomas as a generalization of spherical objects. We classify the weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object in the sense of Krug. For $n=1$, this recovers the classification of weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a spherical object due to Holm, Jorgensen and Yang. We also compute the Koszul-dual model of the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object.

papers.title: High-order positivity-preserving well-balanced schemes: combining flux globalization with modified Patankar deferred correction methods
papers.abstract: Positivity-preserving schemes for hyperbolic balance laws are typically built from the Zhang-Shu limiter and strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta (SSP-RK) time stepping, at the cost of a restrictive time-step condition. The modified Patankar deferred correction (mPDeC) method removes this restriction, offering high-order accuracy, conservation, and unconditional positivity. However, its solution-dependent Patankar weights make the time update nonlinear, so, unlike with RK methods, preserving (steady and moving) equilibria, i.e., well-balancing (WB), is no longer straightforward. In this paper, we construct high-order, WB, positivity-preserving mPDeC schemes by combining mPDeC with a flux-globalization approach. We demonstrate the idea on the one-dimensional shallow water equations, using a WB A-WENO spatial discretization, and introduce a modified local characteristic decomposition that remains stable in the presence of dry states. Numerical experiments on one-dimensional benchmarks confirm that the method satisfies the desired properties.

papers.title: The Calderón operator for time-harmonic Maxwell's equations in closed waveguides
papers.abstract: We consider the time-harmonic Maxwell's equations in a closed, cylindrical waveguide with longitudinal invariant but heterogeneous permittivity and permeability. We consider minimal smoothness assumptions, i.e., the material parameters have to be in $L^\infty$ and the cross section has to be Lipschitz with a possibly non-trivial topology. First, we show that the associated Calderón operator is well-defined and bounded in the natural trace spaces $\mathbf{H}_0^{-1/2}(\operatorname{curl}_Γ;Γ) \to \mathbf{H}_0^{-1/2}(\operatorname{div}_Γ;Γ)$. Second, we consider interior Maxwell problems obtained from using the Calderón operator and analyze their well-posedness. Furthermore, we report some additional results on the location and group velocities of the waveguide wavenumbers.

papers.title: A geometry-independent endpoint estimate for the Littlewood--Paley $g$-function generated by the Poisson semigroup
papers.abstract: We prove a weak $(1,1)$ estimate for the full Poisson Littlewood--Paley $g$-function on every complete Riemannian manifold without boundary, with an explicit universal constant approximately equal to $3.33606$. The estimate requires no curvature restriction, volume doubling, heat kernel bound, or stochastic completeness. The proof combines a precise Poisson maximal inequality with a convex entropy identity; local elliptic regularity identifies the extension to arbitrary real $L^1$ data. As an application, we obtain weak $(1,1)$ estimates for certain spectral multipliers represented by Poisson time derivatives with coefficients in $L^2((0,\infty),dt/t)$.

papers.title: Feeling the generalised rough SABR boundary
papers.abstract: We provide an in-depth analysis of a generalised rough version of the SABR volatility model, widely used in the financial industry. We specifically focus on its behaviour at the origin, whether it can reach it and how fast it may do so.

papers.title: Surjective maps preserving quasi-nilpotence of products of operators
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space and let $\mathcal B(X)$ the full algebra of all bounded linear operator on $X$. In this paper, we give a complete characterization of surjective maps $φ:\mathcal B(X)\to\mathcal B(X)$ satisfying \[ r(AB)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad r(φ(A)φ(B))=0 \qquad(A,B\in\mathcal B(X)). \] Without assuming additivity, injectivity, or continuity, we show that there exists a function $γ: B(X)\mapsto \C \setminus\{0\}$ such that the map $φ$ takes one of the following forms: 1. there exists a bounded linear or conjugate-linear, invertible operator $S:X\to X$ such that : \label{eq:direct} φ(A)=γ(A)SAS^{-1},\qquad \text{ for all } \quad A\in B(X), 2. the space $X$ is reflexive and there exists a bounded linear or conjugate-linear, invertible operator $S:X^*\to X$ such that \label{eq:dual} φ(A)=γ(A)SA^*S^{-1},\qquad \text{ for all } \quad A\in B(X).

papers.title: The space of polarized compactifications of an affine variety
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a normal affine variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Through the lens of non-Archimedean geometry, we study the space of polarized compactifications of $X$, consisting of pairs $(\bar X, D)$ where $\bar X$ is a normal projective variety containing $X$ as a dense open subset, and $D$ is an effective ample $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor with support equal to the complement of $X$ in $\bar X$. We identify this space with a natural class of functions--the Fubini--Study functions--on the Berkovich analytification of $X$. Through a Rees correspondence, we also give a bijection with the space of homogeneous $\mathbb{Q}$-valued, finitely generated negative non-Archimedean norms (or filtrations) on the coordinate ring of $X$. Using the above identifications, we equip the space of polarized compactifications, and numerical classes thereof, with natural metrics and identify the metric completions. The latter include a space of continuous plurisubharmonic functions in the sense of Chambert-Loir and Ducros, and a space of birational curve classes as studied by Dang and Favre.

papers.title: Modules and operator rings of Reynolds algebras
papers.abstract: We develop a module theory for weighted Reynolds algebras by constructing an associa?tive ring that records the algebra action and the module operator. The categories of left and right Reynolds modules are equivalent to the corresponding module categories over this ring, and their tensor products agree under these equivalences. We construct free Reynolds modules and give an explicit graded description of the operator ring for idempotent classical Reynolds operators fixing the identity. When the Reynolds operator on the algebra is bijective, modules with bijective module operators correspond to differential modules satisfying an invertibility condition. The operator ring transfers the Hom-tensor adjunction, Morita theory and derived functors to Reynolds modules. Explicit computations over a field show that the identity operator gives an operator ring of global dimension one, whereas the zero operator gives one of infinite global dimension.

papers.title: On the uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for the Motsch-Tadmor model
papers.abstract: We consider the Motsch-Tadmor model, a modification of the Cucker-Smale model for flocking dynamics that incorporates asymmetric communication weights. In the case of uniformly positive interactions, we consider the validity problem for the limiting kinetic equation, proving a uniform-in-time propagation of chaos result in the moving frame given by the consensus velocities. The result is obtained by studying the reversibility of the communication weights and by implicitly characterizing the asymptotic consensus.

papers.title: Finite Time Noncollapsing Kähler-Ricci Flow: Gaussian Type Heat Kernel, Gromov-Hausdorff Limits
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study heat kernel estimates along the Kähler-Ricci flow with finite time noncollapsing singularities over a compact Kähler manifold. The starting point is the type-II scalar-curvature estimate, which gives the natural parabolic scale $r\lesssim T-t$ near the singular time. By combining the distance distortion and space-time cut-off estimates of Bamler--Zhang with entropy, mean-value inequality, and conjugate heat-kernel estimates, we obtain two-sided Gaussian bounds and gradient bounds that are uniform on this scale. Under the global type-I scalar-curvature estimate, the same estimates hold on every scale. We then use these estimates and the monotonicity of the $W_1$-distance between conjugate heat flows to construct a canonical singular-time pseudo-distance. The distances $d_t$ (induced by $ω(t)$) converge uniformly to this pseudo-distance. Its metric quotient is the unique Gromov--Hausdorff limit. Finally, we apply Bamler's theory and the recent work of Hallgren--Zhang to obtain the following. Every fixed-base-point type-I blow-up admits a subsequential metric-flow limit whose time slices are singular shrinking Kähler--Ricci soliton spaces with normal complex-analytic and log-terminal structure, unique tangent cones, and a polarized Fano fibration. For moving base points, the limiting metric flow, equipped with its limiting conjugate heat flow, is a metric soliton precisely under an entropy-pinching condition.

papers.title: Generalized Cluster Algebra Homomorphisms Induced by Cluster Tube Embeddings
papers.abstract: We relate multiplication formulas for regular modules in coefficient-free acyclic affine cluster algebras with skew-symmetric exchange matrices to the imaginary exchange relations of Reading-Stella. Introducing a parameter $z$ into the construction of Zhou-Zhu, we define a weighted cluster character on cluster tubes that satisfies generalized exchange relations of type $C_{n-1}$ and yields a bijection between indecomposable rigid objects and cluster variables. Using the multiplication formulas and difference property of Ding-Xiao-Xu, we show that non-homogeneous tube embeddings induce injective homomorphisms into ordinary affine cluster algebras under $z\mapsto X_δ$. Comparison with Reading-Stella's relations identifies $X_δ$ with the corresponding theta function, giving a representation-theoretic interpretation of the generalized exchange parameter.

papers.title: Inverse Wave Problems on Graphs
papers.abstract: We study inverse wave problems on finite graphs from time-dependent measurements on a prescribed set of vertices. With the graph geometry known, we consider recovery of either the initial signal or the vertex wave speeds when the other is given. Initial-signal recovery is characterized by observability of the associated finite-dimensional system, while a single experiment determines the vertex wave speeds under a zero forcing condition and a natural nonharmonicity assumption. We establish stability estimates for both recovery problems, develop a nonlinear least-squares reconstruction method, and extend the results to positively weighted graphs. Numerical simulations illustrate the reconstruction and examine the effects of observation geometry, time horizon, coefficient localization, and measurement noise on its performance.
