These conditions require no Lyapunov function and no stability of the Markov transitions, and allow for non-compact state spaces: confinement is provided by the potential functions. Our perturbation bounds hold in total variation and in the Kolmogorov norm; for the latter, we extend the Hardy--Krause variation and the Koksma--Hlawka inequality to unbounded domains. Our perturbation theory is applied to derive time-uniform bounds for linearized Kalman filters, Euler schemes for partially observed diffusions and nudged state-space models, as well as high-probability error bounds, uniform over whole trajectories, for particle filters and, more generally, for mean field particle methods such as sequential Monte Carlo and diffusion Monte Carlo algorithms.

papers.title: Augmentation curve for torus knots
papers.abstract: We prove a version of topological recursion for the correlation differentials of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials of torus knots on the corresponding augmentation curves, following the proposal of Gu, Jockers, Klemm, and Soroush. To this end, we explicitly construct the spectral curve from the so-called auxiliary curve of Brini, Eynard, and Mariño and prove that it coincides with the augmentation curve for every torus knot with coprime $(r,s)$. Finally, our version of topological recursion proves the higher-genus closed-string prediction of the Aganagic--Vafa conjecture for all torus knot augmentation curves.

papers.title: $PF$-well-filtered spaces
papers.abstract: This paper solves two open problems concerning the well-filteredness of topological spaces. The first, due to Shen, Xi and Zhao\cite{shen2023further}, asks whether a space must be open well-filtered whenever its upper space is so; the answer is negative; the Hofmann-Lawson space provides a counterexample. The second, posed by Li, Yuan and Zhao\cite{li2020unified}, inquires whether $PF$-well-filteredness and $PF$- sobriety are equivalent under the assumption of local compactness; we answer it in the affirmative. Subsequently, we give characterizations of $PF$-sobriety and $PF$-well-filteredness for $T_0$ spaces, respectively. On the basis of the characterizations, we obtain the following result: $PF$-sobriety and $PF$-well-filteredness coincide on the Rudin spaces, which extends the previously established equivalence for locally compact spaces, as every locally compact space is a Rudin space. Furthermore, we give a counterexample to show that for nonempty $T_0$ topological spaces $X$ and $Y$, if $Y$ is a $PF$-well-filtered ($PF$-sober) space, then the function space consisting of all continuous maps from $X$ to $Y$ equipped with the Isbell topology may not be a $PF$-well-filtered ($PF$-sober) space even when $X$ is a core-compact space. We also prove that if the function space comprising all continuous maps from nonempty $X$ to $Y$ endowed with the Isbell topology is $PF$-well-filtered ($PF$-sober), then $Y$ is also $PF$-well-filtered ($PF$-sober) even though $PF$-sobriety and $PF$-well-filteredness are not preserved under retracts. Finally, we show that the reflective hull of the category of $PF$-well-filtered ($PF$-sober) spaces with continuous maps in $TOP_0$ is $TOP_0$.

papers.title: Generalized Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv Constants for finite abelian groups of rank three
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with exponent $\exp(G)$. For positive integer $k$, the generalized Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant, denoted by $\mathsf s_{k\exp(G)}(G)$ is the least integer $\ell$ such that every sequence of length at least $\ell$ over $G$ has a zero-sum subsequence of length $k\exp(G)$. In this paper, we prove that, for any $n\ge 1$, \[\mathsf s_{3\cdot 2^n}(C_{2^n}^3)=6\cdot 2^n-3 \quad\text{and}\quad \mathsf s_{4\cdot 3^n}(C_{3^n}^3)=7\cdot 3^n-3. \] This completes all the remaining cases in the study of $\mathsf s_{kq}(C_q^3)$, where $q$ is a prime power and $k\ge 3$. As a consequence, for every $k\ge 3$, we have \[ \mathsf s_{kn}(C_n^3)=(k+3)n+O(\frac{n}{\log n}). \] This verifies a conjecture of Kubertin asymptotically. Our approach combines the previous group ring techniques and a recent powerful generalization of the Chevalley-Warning and Ax-Katz theorems introduced by Grynkiewicz

papers.title: A Proof of the Jung-Kim Conjecture on the Centers of Walled Brauer Algebras
papers.abstract: We give a unified account of the five families of Khovanov arc algebras $K_n^m$, $K_n^{-\infty}$, $K_n^{+\infty}$, $K_n^\infty$ and $K_\infty^\infty$ in the framework of level-two tensor product categorifications, making explicit a perspective familiar to specialists. Our main application is a proof of the Jung--Kim conjecture: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the centre of every walled Brauer algebra is generated by supersymmetric polynomials in its Jucys--Murphy elements. We also give a homogeneous basis of the centre in terms of arc diagrams, for the grading induced by $K_\infty^\infty$. The proof combines a calculation of the arc-algebra centre with an explicit comparison of central actions under the Brundan--Stroppel Morita equivalence and Brundan-Kleshchev isomorphism. Along the way, we explain the relation between $K_n^{-\infty}$ and classical super duality, and identify $K_n^{-\infty}$ and $K_n^{+\infty}$ as Ringel duals. We also revisit mixed Schur--Weyl duality for general linear Lie superalgebras within the same framework.

papers.title: Lattice coverings by parallelotopes containing cube vertices
papers.abstract: We investigate when a parallelotope containing vertices of the unit cube $Q_n=[0,1]^n$ covers $\Bbb R^n$ by integer translates. We prove the covering property for every parallelepiped containing five vertices of $Q_3$, and, in any dimension, for every parallelotope containing a facet of $Q_n$ and one vertex of the opposite facet. As a consequence, we obtain the sharp bound $1/n$ for the volume of a pyramid contained in $Q_n$ with a parallelotope base. We also give an alternative proof of this bound.

papers.title: Density of repelling periodic points for cubic rational maps
papers.abstract: We prove the repelling-density conjecture for cubic rational maps over $\mathbf C_p$: for every prime $p$, the classical Julia set is the closure of the classical repelling periodic points. By Bézivin's theorem, it suffices to prove that a nonempty classical Julia set contains a classical repelling periodic point. The case $p\geq5$ follows from known results for tame maps, so we treat residue characteristics two and three. We argue by contraposition, assuming that the map has no classical repelling periodic points. Maps with potential good reduction already have empty classical Julia set. Otherwise, we conjugate the map to an explicit normalized form and analyze its coefficients. In each case, we obtain coefficient restrictions and establish a uniform bound on the spherical derivatives of all iterates. This bound implies equicontinuity on the classical projective line and hence emptiness of the classical Julia set.

papers.title: Reducing the Cost of Qudit State Preparation by Learning a Sparse Structure for SNAP Gates
papers.abstract: Preparing quantum states in bosonic qudits with SNAP--Displacement sequences requires both optimizing the gate parameters and deciding which Fock levels should be controlled by each SNAP gate. A fully parameterized ansatz assigns an independent phase to every Fock level in every gate, leading to a number of phases that grows steeply. This constitutes a problem for short to medium term systems as controlling many phases requires complex control pulses which are subject to increased control errors. Previous work reduced this cost by restricting the trainable phases to predefined sparse patterns, such as a diagonal or a grid, which however may not be optimal for a specific target state. In this work, we address this limitation by introducing a method that learns which phases are needed together with their values, using a differentiable mask. A sparsity penalty encourages the removal of unnecessary phases, while temperature annealing gradually turns the masks into binary decisions. We compare the proposed method with fully parameterized and predefined sparse ansatzes on Fourier and Haar-random target states. The evaluation considers both the minimum number of phases required to reach different infidelity thresholds and the overall trade-off between fidelity and phases required, measured through Pareto frontiers and hypervolume. The results show that learning the location of the phases together with their values provides competitive or improved fidelity--resource trade-offs, although the advantage depends on the target state and qudit dimension.

papers.title: Finite-Frequency Boson-Number Bounds Across the Quantum Rabi Transition
papers.abstract: We consider the quantum Rabi model, a fundamental model of quantum optics describing a two-level system coupled to a bosonic mode, including counter-rotating terms. In the limit of large separation between the two-level transition frequency and the bosonic mode frequency, the model exhibits a quantum phase transition at a critical coupling strength. Although the model is exactly solvable, simple analytic expressions for important physical quantities are generally unavailable. We derive rigorous upper and lower bounds for the ground-state energy and boson occupation number across the quantum phase transition at finite frequency ratios. Our results characterize the subcritical, critical, and supercritical regimes and establish the scaling behavior of the boson occupation near the critical point. Exact numerical diagonalization demonstrates the tightness of the derived bounds, while the resulting finite-frequency inequalities provide experimentally testable predictions for trapped-ion quantum simulators.

papers.title: Estimators from Convex Geometries of the Simplex
papers.abstract: We unify several geometries of the probability simplex under one principle, their generation by a potential: convex potentials produce the Bregman divergences and dually flat structures of information geometry, and the exponentially concave potentials of Pal and Wong produce the logarithmic divergences and their projectively flat structures. Each structure carries a duality between maximum entropy and minimum divergence and, with it, a projection principle for estimation: the U-estimators of Eguchi, Komori and Ohara in the first case, the λ-deformed estimators of Wong and Zhang in the second, both governed by a Pythagorean relation and reducing to maximum likelihood in the undeformed limit. We complete the picture with estimators drawn from the third connection the divergence defines, the Levi-Civita one, by minimizing geodesic distance: existence, uniqueness and influence are then controlled by curvature and diameter rather than by flatness. Along the way the Aitchison geometry appears as the logarithmic-barrier instance of the construction at its critical weight, and the symmetrization of the Pal-Wong transport cost, a smoothing of the Hilbert projective metric, is shown to lose the dual pair and to support instead a Huber-type robust center with bounded influence in a geometry of infinite diameter.

papers.title: Generic Mean Curvature Flow With Rough Weights
papers.abstract: We prove the generic existence of mean curvature flows in spaces with rough weights. Our weak solutions are both unit-density Brakke flows and distributional solutions. Such a generic statement is optimal in the sense that we consider weights that are too rough to have well-defined traces on every hypersurface.

papers.title: On the variety of sum of powers of certain complete intersection forms
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a homogeneous polynomial (form). If the annihilator ideal $F^\perp$ is a complete intersection, then $F$ is called as a complete intersection form. For many complete intersection forms, we show that its minimal apolar ideal is a complete intersection and further we show that ${\rm VSP}(F)$ is irreducible and compute its dimension.

papers.title: Spectral Theory for Schrodinger Operators with Interface Transmission Conditions
papers.abstract: Interfaces influence transport across biological membranes, habitat boundaries, and composite media. Motivated by these applications, we study two classes of Schrodinger eigenvalue problems with transmission conditions allowing jumps in the solution or its normal derivative. We develop a weighted variational framework that accommodates asymmetric interface coupling and yields self-adjoint realizations in suitable weighted Hilbert spaces. For both problems and their adjoints, we establish discrete spectra, variational eigenvalue characterizations, and eigenfunction completeness in arbitrary spatial dimensions. We prove spectral continuity and identify limiting spectra in singular parameter regimes. We also extend Courant's nodal domain theorem to eigenfunctions that may be discontinuous across the interface. The spectral results further extend to divergence-form elliptic operators under suitable assumptions on the coefficients. These results provide a foundation for analyzing elliptic and parabolic equations with interface transmission conditions.

papers.title: It Takes Two Moments: Rigidity and Limits of Continuous Encoders for Over-the-Air Computation
papers.abstract: We study over-the-air computation of functions, such as empirical variance, formed by combining two separately postprocessed sums of locally transformed observations. We consider continuous encoders subject to pointwise peak-power constraints over a single use of a complex multiple-access channel. With four or more transmitters, we identify conditions under which exact noiseless recovery forces every continuous encoder collection into a common affine structure that preserves both sums, reducing infinite-dimensional encoder design to selecting a finite set of coefficients. To quantify resilience against channel noise, we introduce a robustness score that measures the separation of noiseless received aggregates relative to variations in the desired function value. Within this characterized encoder family, we formulate robustness maximization as an exact convex semi-infinite program, eliminating rank constraints without a relaxation gap, and construct a decoder that attains the minimum uniform noise-amplification constant. For several function classes, including empirical variance, we derive closed-form robustness-optimal encoders and scores. Under mild regularity conditions, we also establish sharp limits on the Gaussian mean squared error at high signal-to-noise ratios and show how using the input distribution reduces average error at the expense of uniform robustness.

papers.title: Rectangular Symmetry for Catalan Functions
papers.abstract: Katabolizable tableaux provide a combinatorial formula for the Schur coefficients of Catalan functions. We prove that a tableau involution preserves katabolizability under antidiagonal reflection of any upper root ideal. This involution complements shape and content in a fixed rectangle and preserves charge. We obtain a bijective proof of the rectangular symmetry of these coefficients.

papers.title: On the Solution Sets of the Cone-Volume Map
papers.abstract: For a fixed set $U=(u_1,\ldots,u_m)$ of outer unit normals, we consider the cone-volume map which associates to a vector of support numbers $b\in\mathbb R^m_{> 0}$ the cone-volume vector $γ\in\mathbb R^m$ of the polytope \[ P(U,b)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:U^\top x\leq b\}. \] We study its fibers $S(U,γ)$ over prescribed cone-volume vectors $γ$, with particular emphasis on finiteness and non-uniqueness. We give characterizations of the irreducibility of $U$ in terms of properties of the cone-volume map and its solution sets. In particular, for irreducible $U$, we show that $S(U,γ)$ is finite for all $γ$ outside a set of measure zero in the cone-volume cone, and we give an explicit upper bound for its cardinality. In the planar case, we prove that $S(U,γ)$ has semialgebraic dimension at most one for arbitrary $U$. Moreover, for every $U\in\mathcal{U}(2,m)$ with $m\geq 4$, there exists a cone-volume vector $γ$ for which $S(U,γ)$ contains at least two distinct elements. As a consequence, there exist two distinct smooth planar convex bodies with the same cone-volume measure. Finally, for $U$ in general position, we show that the number of solutions is odd for every cone-volume vector outside the exceptional set.

papers.title: The Bardos-Tartar Conjecture for the Navier-Stokes Equations
papers.abstract: We consider the incompressible viscous Navier-Stokes equations in dimension $d=2,3$ with periodic boundary conditions and time-independent external forcing. When $d=2$, the Bardos-Tartar conjecture asks whether the set of solutions at any given positive time is dense in the Hilbert subspace of $L^2$ consisting of mean-zero divergence-free vector fields, with respect to the strong $L^2$ norm. We prove the Bardos-Tartar conjecture and, more generally, its analogue for the hyperviscous Navier-Stokes equations studied by Guo-Titi. In addition, for $d=2,3$ we show that any given initial condition is either backwards-extendable (i) for all values of viscosity $ν>0$, or (ii) only for viscosities that belong to a Lebesgue-null subset of $\mathbb{R}_+$. When (i) holds, we show the initial condition and forcing must be real-analytic (in fact, both belong to $D(e^{σA})$ for some $σ>0$, where $A$ is the Stokes operator). Furthermore, we show that (i) is extremely unstable under perturbations. In particular, given any initial condition we show that two Fourier modes can be perturbed so that (ii) holds.

papers.title: Frey-Mazur theorem for semistable elliptic curves over function fields
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a field, let $B/k$ be a smooth projective geometrically integral curve, and put $K=k(B)$. We prove a Frey--Mazur type theorem for nonisotrivial semistable elliptic curves over $K$. More precisely, after fixing the genus of $B$ and the characteristic of $k$, a sufficiently large prime-to-characteristic torsion representation determines the $K$-isogeny class.

papers.title: BOLT: Multi-Bottleneck Bound-Guided Learning for Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling with Time Lags and Resource-Coupled Transport
papers.abstract: Flexible job-shop scheduling becomes resource-coupled when a scarce vehicle fleet moves jobs between stations, because the schedule sets the transport waits. BOLT (bound-oriented learning for transport-coupled scheduling) builds a lower bound from chain, machine-capacity, and fleet-capacity relaxations. The bound equals the makespan at termination, so its per-step changes form a reward that sums to a constant minus the makespan. Because it never exceeds the attainable makespan, each candidate's bound increase is a proven rise of the makespan floor, which the policy reads as a price. The root bound certifies a completed schedule's suboptimality gap without a solver. On industry-motivated 10-module prefabricated-construction instances, explicit transport coupling outperforms a transport-penalty policy in every tested cell where loaded moves occupy at least 66% of fleet time and in none at or below 56%. Across five zero-shot 50- and 80-module production batches, BOLT outperforms the best dispatching-rule pair on four and the penalty policy on the three with long moves. In the three-vehicle 80-module batch, its mean makespan is 13.0% below the best pair and 4.2% below an hour-budget constraint-programming solver whose proven gap averages 34%. BOLT decides in 2.3-5.9 ms per event on one processor core and re-plans a disruption in seconds.

papers.title: On micro-macro derivation of traffic flow models with $(A,B)$-connection and its stability
papers.abstract: We show that $(A,B)$-connections for conservations laws with a flux discontinuity can be obtained as limits of perturbed Follow-the-Leader (FtL) models, and provide continuity and surjectivity of the map associating the perturbation of the dynamics with the flux limiter.

papers.title: Algorithms for computing basins of attraction associated with a rational self-map of the Hopf fibration based on Lyapunov exponents
papers.abstract: The objective of this work is twofold. One, we develop a theory of iteration for complex rational functions so that the problems of overflow and indeterminacy caused by null, or almost null, denominators can be avoided when developing implementations. Second, we present easily implementable methods that allow the calculation of attracting cycles as well as the graphical representation of their basins of attraction. In order to deal with our first goal, we work with homogeneous complex coordinates, and we take the complex projective line as a model, which is expressed as a quotient of the 3-sphere through the Hopf fibration. An irreducible representation of a rational function can now be presented as a Hopf fibration endomorphism. As well as our second goal is concerned, we use Lyapunov functions and exponents to calculate the cycles associated with endomorphisms and to graphically represent the corresponding basins of attraction. We point out that our algorithms are based on the calculation of a finite set of non-negative real constants, and their calculation does not depend on the previous determination of the fixed points or attracting cycles.

papers.title: Imaginary quadratic fields of class number at most 2000
papers.abstract: We determine all imaginary quadratic fields with class number at most 2000, unconditionally: there are 16,453,493 of them, and the largest $|d_K|$ among them is 1,062,350,083. To our knowledge, such a list was previously known only for class number at most 100. We make explicit a recent argument, released by OpenAI and not refereed, that excludes Landau-Siegel zeros: every real zero $β$ of $L(s,χ)$, for a primitive real character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge3$, satisfies $(1-β)\log q\ge5.8\cdot10^{-4}$. An elementary lower bound for $L(1,χ)$ then shows that a field with class number at most 2000 has $|d_K|<1.61\cdot10^{15}$. The fields with $6\cdot2^{28}\le|d_K|\le1.65\cdot10^{15}$ are excluded by Watkins' sieve, and those below are read from the class group tables of Mosunov and Jacobson. As a consequence, the lists of Cremona and Sutherland of imaginary quadratic orders with class number at most 1000, and the counts of Holmin, Jones, Kurlberg, McLeman and Petersen for odd class numbers up to 1999, previously known under the generalized Riemann hypothesis, hold unconditionally. The two steps, the bound for $β$ and the bound for $|d_K|$, are proved in Lean, building on the existing formalization of that argument, and the proofs are checked by two independent kernels. The contributions of AI systems to this work are stated in the paper.

papers.title: A Krause-type recollement for Q-shaped derived categories
papers.abstract: Let k be a commutative noetherian hereditary ring and let Q be a small, Hom-finite, locally bounded k-linear category admitting a Serre functor and satisfying the strong retraction property, with nilpotent pseudo-radical. For every k-algebra A, we construct a recollement of the Q-shaped homo?topy category KQ(A Inj) of objectwise injective Q-shaped modules by its full subcategory Kac Q (A Inj) of exact objects and the Q-shaped derived category DQ(A). The construction uses complete hereditary cotorsion pairs and does not require A to be noetherian. If A is left noetherian, both KQ(A Inj) and Kac Q (A Inj) are compactly generated by special preenvelopes of finitely generat?ed stalk modules. We identify (Kac Q (A Inj))c with the idempotent completion of (KQ(A Inj))c/LI ((DQ(A))c ), where LI is the fully faithful left adjoint of the localization. This paper builds on and generalizes works of Krause and Liu

papers.title: Strong coloring numbers of grids
papers.abstract: For positive integers $n$ and $d$, the $d$-dimensional grid of side length $n$ is the graph $G(n,d)$ with vertex set $[n]^d$, in which two vertices are adjacent if they differ by $1$ in exactly one coordinate and agree in all the other coordinates. We determine, for every fixed $d$, the asymptotic growth in $r$ of the $r$th strong coloring numbers of these grids. More precisely for $n$ large enough, ${\rm scol}_r(G(n,d)) = Ω_d\bigl(r^{d-1}\bigr)$ as $r\to\infty$. This matches an upper bound given by a volume packing argument, which holds more generally for touching graphs of unit balls in $\mathbb R^d$. For the lower bound, we construct in $G(n,d)$ a bramble of order $Ω_d(n^{d-1})$ with each element of radius at most $dn$. This construction was found by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol.

papers.title: Ehrhart positivity for paving positroids
papers.abstract: A central conjecture of Ferroni, Jochemko, and Schröter posits that every positroid is Ehrhart positive. While Ehrhart positivity has recently been verified for notable classes such as lattice path matroids and series-parallel matroids, the general conjecture remains open. In this paper, we prove that the base polytope of any paving positroid has positive Ehrhart coefficients. This establishes a new class of Ehrhart positive positroids and provides substantial evidence supporting this conjecture.

papers.title: Complete homogeneous varieties over a field
papers.abstract: The main objects of this paper are complete homogeneous varieties under the action of a semisimple group $G$ over field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. When the isotropy groups of the geometric points are smooth parabolics, these are classically known as twisted flag varieties and are well studied in the literature. If the smoothness assumption is removed, we get a larger class of varieties which we call as \emph{twisted parabolic varieties}. The main goal of this paper is to study the structure, classification and properties of these varieties. We first understand their structure over a separable closure of $k$ by classifying non-smooth parabolics containing a Borel; this builds on the recently completed classification of such parabolics over an algebraically closed field. Then, via Galois descent we get a combinatorial criterion for such a variety to descend over $k$. We compute the Picard group of twisted parabolic varieties by embedding them into products of twisted flag varieties, study their local rigidity properties and show that they are rational if they have a $k$-rational point for $p \geq 3$. When $k$ is perfect, we show many interesting properties such as existence of a universal purely inseparable cover, transitivity of $k$-rational points under $G(k)$ as well as the existence of a smooth parabolic in the stabilizer of every such point. However, these properties fail if $k$ is imperfect and we demonstrate this with illuminating examples.

papers.title: Continuous representations of the meta Hahn algebra and special functions
papers.abstract: Infinite families of biorthogonal rational functions are constructed using infinite dimensional representations of the three-generated meta Hahn algebra. Continuous Hahn and continuous dual Hahn polynomials are also recovered along the way using an embedding of the Hahn algebra inside the meta Hahn. Rational functions and polynomials arise as transition coefficients between eigenvectors and generalized eigenvectors, and their algebraic properties follow naturally from the relations of the meta Hahn algebra. Finally, biorthogonality relations are established for the rational functions introduced in the paper.

papers.title: Smoothness of Shortest Isogenies to Frobenius Conjugates
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be chosen uniformly from the geometric isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ and $δ_E$ be the minimum degree of isogenies from $E$ to its Frobenius conjugate $E^{(p)}$. We prove the smoothness of $δ_E$ and hence affirm Wesolowski's $p^{1/3+o(1)}$ attack on the supersingular endomorphism ring problem is unconditional.

papers.title: A sharp survival threshold for branching Brownian motion in a self-generated resource environment
papers.abstract: We study branching Brownian motion in a resource environment created by the particles themselves. Particles reproduce at rate $β$ times the resource nearby, resource is consumed at rate $c$ times the number of particles nearby, and each death returns resource mass $m$. Let $θ=βm/c$, which represents the number of births supported by resource from one corpse, assuming perfect efficiency. We prove that the population dies out almost surely if $θ\leq1$, even with perfect recycling $\left(θ=1\right)$. If $θ>1$ and the interaction kernel has finite range and is bounded below at short distances, the population survives with positive probability from every initial state with at least two particles, or with one particle and some resource. The threshold does not depend on the diffusivity, the death rate or the interaction kernel. We prove extinction for $θ\leq 1$ by showing the total mass in the system to be a supermartingale. The proof of survival rests on two estimates: a large colony grows if it consumes its corpses with little waste, and a dense colony recycles corpses efficiently. Together these imply that a large, dense colony grows with exponentially high probability, and a standard doubling and restart argument then yields survival.

papers.title: Multiplicative Path Weights in Networks: From Katz Connectivity to Mean First-Passage Times
papers.abstract: Signal dispersion, stress propagation in interbank systems, and transmission probabilities in epidemic and reliability models are all captured by studying paths on directed graphs where the path weight is defined as the product of its edge weights. Connectivity in such networks is naturally quantified by aggregating these multiplicative path weights across nodes. This paper provides a comprehensive treatise on connectivity and ranking measures based on multiplicative path weights. We demonstrate how standard all-path connectivity, such as the standard Katz centrality, can be extended beyond its classical spectral threshold. In addition, we derive closed-form expressions for connectivity based on first-hit paths and introduce a new version of Katz centrality. Furthermore, for random edge weights, we derive resolvent-based expressions for the first and second moments, alongside variance bounds, under a path-indexed coupling framework. Finite irreducible Markov chains are a subclass of the models studied, and we show that the scaled matrix of first-hit path probabilities is the probability-generating function for first-passage and return times, and that differentiation yields the classical first-passage times. Numerical examples illustrate the application of our results in a variety of settings.

papers.title: Global Well-Posedness for the 3-D Inviscid Oldroyd-B Model with Fractional Stress Diffusion
papers.abstract: We study the 3-D incompressible inviscid Oldroyd-B model with fractional stress diffusion \((-Δ)^βτ\) and without stress damping. For $β\in (\frac{1}{2},1)$ and $s\in [2β+\frac{1}{2},\frac{5}{2}]$, we establish local well-posedness for initial data $(u_0,τ_0)$ in \(H^s(\mathbb R^3)\), provided that \(\|(u_0,τ_0)\|_{H^β}\) is bounded and \(\|Λ^β(u_0,τ_0)\|_{H^{s-β}}\) is sufficiently small. If, in addition, $β\in(\frac{1}{2},\frac{5}{6}]$, we give a global well-posedness result. Our results complement the work of Constantin, Wu, Zhao and Zhu \cite{ConstantinWuZhaoZhu2021} by treating the Sobolev regularity $s\in[2β+\frac12,\frac{5}{2}]$, below the threshold $s>\frac52$ considered there. We also provide an $\ell^2$ alternative to the high-frequency $\ell^1$ summability condition in the framework of Wu and Zhao \cite{WuZhao2022}.

papers.title: Smale's mean value constant and admissible univalent Blaschke pairs
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the class of polynomials $P$ of degree at least $2$ with $P(0)=0$, $P'(0)=1$, let $S(P)=\min_{P'(c)=0}|P(c)/c|$ and let $\mathcal{M}=\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}}S(P)$ be Smale's mean value constant. Smale proved that $\mathcal{M}\le4$, observed that $\mathcal{M}\ge 1$, and asked whether $\mathcal{M}=1$. We show that $\mathcal{M}$ coincides with $$ \mathcal{B}=\sup\frac1{B(0)}, $$ the supremum running over pairs $(W,B)$ in which $W$ is a normalised univalent map of the standard unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ and $B$ is a finite Blaschke product with $B(0)>0$ such that $WB$ is locally univalent in $\mathbb{D}$. Smale's question is therefore a problem in univalent function theory. We also introduce the degree-restricted constants $\mathcal{B}_d$ for $B$ with $\mathrm{deg} B \le d$ and show that $$1.1018586788\ldots=\sqrt{\frac{8081}{6656}} \le \mathcal{B}_1 < \sqrt{\frac{7}{5}}=1.1832159566\ldots$$ This implies that $\mathcal{M}>1.1018$ and we also show that there are polynomials of arbitrarily large degree with $S(P)>1.1018$.

papers.title: Fixed-spinor radial solutions of a perturbed Euclidean spinorial Yamabe equation
papers.abstract: We study the perturbed Euclidean spinorial Yamabe equation \[ D_{g_{\mathbb R^n}}ψ = \frac n2\bigl(1+\varepsilon K(x)\bigr) |ψ|^{2^*-2}ψ \qquad\text{on }\mathbb R^n,\quad n\ge2, \]where $2^*:=2n/(n-1)$, $\varepsilon>0$ is a small parameter and $K$ is a prescribed radial function. We establish a finite-dimensional reduction within a radial spinor space determined by a fixed unit spinor, reducing the problem to the analysis of a function of the dilation parameter. Under suitable assumptions on $K$, we obtain explicit existence criteria for solutions with this prescribed spinorial structure, together with a multiplicity criterion yielding solutions associated with distinct scales. These criteria are expressed in terms of the behavior of $K$ at the origin and weighted integral quantities.

papers.title: Limits of adaptive two-way linear postprocessing in six-state quantum key distribution
papers.abstract: Two-way classical communication improves the noise tolerance of quantum key distribution, but the limits of adaptive parity processing remain unclear. For the six-state protocol with equal three-basis error rate $p\in[p_*,1/2]$, where $p_*=(5-\sqrt5)/10\simeq27.64\%$, we construct a single compatible collective attack that defeats a broad class of linear postprocessing. Each public message may be a linear function of the sender's raw key, chosen adaptively from the public history. For every finite input length and every accepted transcript of positive probability, Eve's optimal probability of recovering any linear function of Alice's raw key is at least Bob's. Consequently, reliable agreement on a linear final key is incompatible with secrecy. The same conclusion holds for arbitrary publicly seeded privacy amplification after reliable recovery of a linear candidate. The proof conditions on the complete transcript, which restricts the two raw keys to affine subspaces. A local degradation of Eve's state, a known Rényi-entropy comparison, and a coset-probability inequality then give the recovery comparison. Both inequalities are proved in self-contained appendices. The result allows block splitting, regrouping, nonzero-syndrome selection, and adaptive linear reconciliation.

papers.title: Periodic conditional measurements on a photonic chip
papers.abstract: Quantum measurements not only extract information but also reshape quantum evolution through measurement backaction. Here, we investigate periodic conditional measurements, in which coherent evolution is repeatedly interrupted by local measurements. We show that the bright and dark modes of the conditional evolution operator provide a unified spectral description of both the post-selected final state along no-detection trajectories and the statistics of detection events. Using a three-dimensional photonic chip, we demonstrate on-demand state engineering through dark-mode preservation and bright-mode selection, enabling the protection of topological corner states and excited-state shelving. We further observe the predicted transition of the total detection probability on an effectively infinite one-dimensional lattice and identify its microscopic origin in Floquet near-dark modes. These results establish periodic conditional measurements as a general framework for engineering conditional quantum states and manipulating event-detection statistics in monitored quantum dynamics.

papers.title: Semiclassical Band Splitting in the Infinite Chern Band Model
papers.abstract: We study the two lowest Bloch bands of the infinite Chern band model in the semiclassical limit. When the Berry curvature parameter is an odd multiple of \(π\), we derive an explicit asymptotic formula for their exponentially small splitting, uniformly over the Brillouin torus. The proof combines Agmon estimates and WKB approximations for a matrix Schrödinger operator whose lowest potential eigenvalue has two wells. Geometric properties of the Agmon distance allow us to compute the leading tunneling coefficients by the method of stationary phase. We provide numerical computations to illustrate the asymptotic formula and support the conjecture that the two bands remain separated for other values of the Berry curvature parameter.

papers.title: Descending Everest with First-Order Oracles: Oracle Complexity of Convex Optimization under $(L_0,L_1)$-Smoothness
papers.abstract: For convex $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth functions, the curvature may grow together with the gradient norm. Therefore, even when $\|x^0-x^*\|\le R$, the gradient and the optimality gap at the starting point may be exponentially large in $L_1R$, and the bound $\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}$, known for the accelerated method on functions with Lipschitz gradient, no longer describes the complexity of the problem. We determine the oracle complexity of this class for arbitrary deterministic first-order methods: for $L_0R^2/\varepsilon\ge1$, the optimal number of oracle calls $N$ satisfies $1+N=\widetildeΘ(\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+L_1R)$. The upper bound reads $O(\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+(1+L_1R)\log(2+L_1R))$: the method first passes through the large-gradient regime in $O(1+L_1R)$ iterations with an inexact line search, and then the standard accelerated method with a constant stepsize takes over. The lower bound is obtained by means of chains and the orthogonal invariance principle on functions conjugate to strongly convex functions on a polytope. If the initial optimality gap is at most $4\varepsilon$, the optimal bound becomes $1+N=\widetildeΘ(\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+(L_1R)^{2/3})$.

papers.title: An Alternating Minimization Algorithm for Federated Sparse Orthogonal Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop an alternating minimization algorithm for federated sparse orthogonal nonnegative matrix factorization (ONMF) with emphases on controlling client drift. To reduce communication frequency, clients perform multiple local updates between communication rounds, biasing updates toward their respective local objectives and giving rise to client drift, particularly under data heterogeneity. In federated sparse ONMF, global nonsmooth regularization further complicates drift control, as proximal mappings generally do not commute with averaging. To address these challenges, we develop an effective optimization algorithm that introduces variable splitting to decouple proximal operator evaluation from communication, allowing clients to handle joint sparsity regularization locally. In addition, the algorithm incorporates a correction term into the local gradients to adjust the update directions and mitigate client drift. We theoretically establish that the proposed algorithm achieves sublinear convergence to a bounded residual error under some mild conditions. Numerical experiments demonstrate favorable convergence behavior on a synthetic dataset and competitive clustering performance on real-world multi-view datasets.

papers.title: Curvature-Distortion Numbers of Graphs: Prescribed Lin--Lu--Yau Curvature Lower Bounds
papers.abstract: We study an optimization problem for weighted Lin--Lu--Yau curvature. Given a graph $G=(V,E)$ and a prescribed lower curvature bound $k\ge0$, we ask for the smallest multiplicative distortion \[ \Dist(w):=\frac{\sup_{e\in E}w_e}{\inf_{e\in E}w_e} \] of the edge weights needed to make every edge have curvature at least $k$. This leads to the family \[ \DN_{\LLY}^{k}(G) := \inf\bigl\{ \Dist(w): κ_{\LLY}^{w}(e)\ge k \text{ for every }e\in E(G) \bigr\}, \] which extends the nonnegative-curvature invariant introduced in our preceding paper \cite{Xia2026InvariantI}. The edge weights change the transition probabilities, while the combinatorial graph distance remains fixed. Positive prescribed curvature leads to a fundamental distinction from the case $k=0$. If $G$ is a connected locally finite infinite graph and $k>0$, then \[ \DN_{\LLY}^{k}(G)=\infty. \] Thus no finite multiplicative distortion of the edge weights can impose a uniform positive curvature lower bound on such a graph. For a finite tree $T$ with $m$ edges, such weights exist exactly when $k\le2/m$. We prove that the minimum distortion is attained by a weight unique up to scaling, and that the normalized minimizer and its distortion depend continuously and nondecreasingly on $k$. We then extend the finite-tree theory to general connected graphs. As an application, we characterize the graphs of girth at least six for which finite $k$-distortion is possible.

papers.title: Good stratifications of non-degenerate locally tame complete intersection varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that non-degenerate locally tame complete intersection varieties admit good stratifications. As an application, we study variation of the Milnor fibrations in pencils associated with non-degenerate hypersurface singularities.

papers.title: The Sharp Scale Inequality for the Schatten Trace Class
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the metric cotype $2$ inequality for the Schatten trace class $S_{1}$ at the optimal order of the scaling parameter. More precisely, for every integer $n\geq 1$, every even integer $m\geq 4$, and every mapping $f:\mathbb{Z}_{m}^{n}\to S_{1}$, the following holds \begin{align*} &\left(\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}_{x}\left\|f\left(x+\frac{m}{2}e_{j}\right)-f(x)\right\|_{1}^{2}\right)^{1/2}\\ \leq&\left(3\sqrt{70}\,m+6\sqrt{n}\right)\left(\mathbb{E}_{x,\varepsilon}\left\|f(x+\varepsilon)-f(x)\right\|_{1}^{2}\right)^{1/2}, \end{align*} where $x$ and $\varepsilon$ are independently uniform on $\mathbb{Z}_{m}^{n}$ and $\{-1,0,1\}^{n}$, respectively. The order $\sqrt{n}$ is necessary for any fixed metric cotype constant. This settles the optimal scaling problem for the Schatten trace class posed by Mendel and Naor \cite[Section 8]{MN} (see also \cite[Question 3]{GMN}).

papers.title: Restarted Fixed-Point Acceleration of Proximal ADMM for Capped-$\ell_1$ Penalized Optimization
papers.abstract: We consider box-constrained optimization with a convex, Lipschitz continuous loss function that may be nonsmooth and a capped-$\ell_1$ penalty. Exploiting the convex branch representation of the capped-$\ell_1$ penalty, we construct an associated nonexpansive fixed-point mapping for each branch and, based on these mappings, propose a restarted accelerated proximal alternating direction method of multipliers (RA-pADMM). The resulting algorithm consists of a preliminary branch identification phase and a subsequent accelerated phase based on either the Halpern or fast Krasnosel'skiĭ--Mann iteration, together with a sufficient decrease restart mechanism. We prove that the preliminary phase terminates after finitely many iterations and that only finitely many branch updates are accepted during the subsequent phase. The primal iterates and proximal outputs converge to a common lifted stationary point, which is also a $ν$-strong local minimizer of the corresponding cardinality penalized problem. Moreover, the Halpern and fast Krasnosel'skiĭ--Mann variants achieve nonergodic $O(k^{-1})$ and asymptotic $o(k^{-1})$ convergence rates, respectively, for both the objective value gap and the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker residual associated with the final branch. Numerical experiments on sparse recovery and real data classification problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed RA-pADMM algorithm.

papers.title: Lifetime-unified quadratic and cubic approximations of fluorescence peak time for a time-domain diffuse-light response
papers.abstract: We study the temporal maximum of a boundary response generated by a coupled diffusion system in a half-space with Robin boundary conditions and a point fluorophore. The fluorescence lifetime enters through a one-sided exponential time convolution. Previous peak-time approximations were derived under separate short- and long-lifetime scalings. We construct a single reduced peak-time formula for every positive ratio of lifetime to the intrinsic width of the transport peak, thereby describing the transition between these regimes without switching formulas. Starting from a known large-distance approximation of the zero-lifetime response, we normalize at its unique maximum and approximate its logarithm quadratically. The resulting scalar mode equation has a unique solution, expressed through the inverse scaled complementary error function. Its endpoint expansions recover the leading structures of the earlier approximations in the corresponding joint large-distance regimes. A cubic correction accounts for the leading local asymmetry. Under a stated bound on the normalized cubic coefficient, we prove uniqueness of its positive mode and agreement with the exact reduced-profile peak expansion through second order in the lifetime. A conditional peak-location stability estimate is combined with a decomposition into transport-profile and local truncation errors. Numerical comparisons with the full diffusion response support the accuracy of the construction. The lifetime-unified formula is distinguished from the fixed-geometry, infinite-lifetime limit, in which the transport tail yields a different peak-time growth law.

papers.title: Casimir forces on suspended thin dielectric membranes covered with graphene
papers.abstract: We investigate the Casimir force on thin suspended dielectric layers covered with graphene, both theoretically and experimentally. Thermal effects of the Casimir force on graphene occur at separations significantly smaller compared to ordinary metals and dielectrics. At such small separations, the Casimir force is sufficiently strong to be measured experimentally. However, the presence of substrates to support the graphene significantly reduces the enhancement. We show theoretically that replacing the solid substrate beneath graphene with a thin dielectric membrane partially restores this strong thermal dependence. One of the interacting objects is a solid gold plate. The other object is a suspended dielectric membrane made of either 15 nm of silicon oxide or 13 nm silicon nitride, covered with graphene. At a separation of $\sim$500 nm, theoretical predictions yield changes in the Casimir pressure of up to 54 % and 40 % for silicon oxide and silicon nitride, respectively, when the temperature is increased from 10 K to 294 K. Measurements were performed for graphene on a suspended silicon nitride membrane at room temperature, using a gold-coated sphere attached to a cantilever as the force sensor. The measured force gradient is consistent with the theoretical prediction, although the thermal dependence could not be resolved, in part because of uncertainties in the optical properties of silicon nitride. Replacing a bulk substrate with a thin dielectric membrane covered with graphene provides a substantial reduction of the Casimir force, which may facilitate the stable operation of neutral nanomechanical elements at small separations.

papers.title: Accurate gap control of 3D-integrated superconducting quantum circuits using asymmetric indium architecture and multi-angle flip-chip bonding
papers.abstract: Flip-chip 3D integration is a key enabling technology for overcoming the routing and layout constraints of planar superconducting quantum processors, but it requires accurate and uniform control of the inter-chip spacing while preserving qubit coherence. In conventional processes, thick indium bumps are deposited symmetrically on both chips, while dedicated spacers are introduced to limit the residual tilt. Here, we present a flip-chip bonding process based on an asymmetric indium architecture, combining $20\,μ\mathrm{m}$ thick indium bumps on the control chip with $200\,\mathrm{nm}$ thin indium pads on the qubit chip. Using electrical and microwave measurements, we demonstrate low resistance and low loss indium interconnects, and show that transmon qubits integrated with this process reach relaxation and coherence times of $T_1=(159\pm14)\,μ\mathrm{s}$ and $T_{\mathrm{2,echo}}=(294\pm42)\,μ\mathrm{s}$, respectively, comparable to planar devices. Combined with a multi angle compression procedure that suppresses systematic tilt, this approach reduces the average post bonding tilt to $(20\pm12)\,μ\mathrm{rad}$. These results establish an asymmetric indium architecture combined with multi angle compression as a robust, coherence preserving route toward 3D-integrated superconducting quantum processors.

papers.title: Strict unimodality of the exact time-domain diffuse-light response under a Robin boundary condition
papers.abstract: Time-domain boundary measurements of diffuse light are temporal point-spread functions whose peak position is used as a robust scalar datum in diffuse optical and fluorescence imaging. We consider the exact response generated by a single fluorescent point target in a homogeneous half-space with a Robin boundary condition. The response is a temporal convolution of two diffusion Green-function factors containing a complementary-error-function boundary correction. For every positive diffusion, absorption, depth, and source--target and detector--target distance parameter, and for every nonnegative Robin parameter, we prove that the normalized exact response is a generalized gamma convolution density. Its extension by zero to the negative half-line is bell-shaped. A differentiable small-time expansion, established by sectorial analyticity and Cauchy estimates, together with the sign-change structure of the first two derivatives, excludes tangential critical points and yields a unique peak with strict increase before it and strict decrease after it. The argument is exact and requires no large-distance, source--detector balance, symmetry, restricted-time, or small-parameter assumption. The same conclusion holds after convolution with an exponential fluorescence-lifetime density for every positive lifetime. The key ingredients are an explicit Stieltjes representation of the Robin factor, hyperbolic complete monotonicity, closure of the generalized gamma convolution class, and bell-shape theory. A derivation of the exact half-space model and the differentiated endpoint asymptotics are included in two appendices.

papers.title: Kernel-Based Heterogeneous Mean Field Games on a Continuum Type Space
papers.abstract: This paper studies a class of heterogeneous mean field games on a continuum type space, in which interactions are generated by a Hilbert-Schmidt kernel operator acting on the type-indexed mean state profile. The control set is allowed to be a general closed convex subset of a Euclidean space, and the optimal feedback is characterized through the unique maximizer of the Hamiltonian. For a prescribed mean-field path, the stochastic maximum principle leads to a family of fully coupled forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs) indexed by the agent type. Under Lipschitz conditions and a monotonicity assumption on the reduced coefficients, the frozen FBSDE is globally well posed. We then formulate the consistency problem as a fixed-point problem for the kernel mean-field path. When the operator norm of the interaction kernel is sufficiently small, the resulting map has an invariant ball and is continuous and compact, so that Schauder's theorem yields existence of a mean field Nash equilibrium. Uniqueness follows under an aggregate monotonicity condition adapted to the kernel coupling. A linear-quadratic example illustrates how finite-rank interactions and heterogeneous risk preferences produce coupled collective modes, and yields a spectral smallness condition for existence and an explicit sufficient condition for uniqueness.

papers.title: Dilaton-Axion Wormhole Partition Function Away from the BPS Endpoint
papers.abstract: I determine the leading finite-radius correction to the two-boundary response of a charged axion wormhole near its BPS endpoint. With $δ=a_*^2$, exact radial matching in a product axion--dilaton/saxion system gives a boundary eigenvalue that vanishes as $O(δ)$ and an off-diagonal Hessian entry of order $O(δ^2)$. Their combination produces a cross-boundary covariance linear in $δ$, with a negative first sub-leading correction on the branch studied here. I determine the semiclassical range in which the quadratic approximation remains controlled and identify the first finite-radius angular resonance, $δ^2\log(δ/δ_0)$. Under a uniform rescaling of all active charges, the coefficient of the linear cross-boundary response scales as the inverse square of the charge scale. I then average the inverse response over the chiral Gaussian ensemble describing the BPS endpoint. Boundary reduction preserves the hard-edge index. Multiplication by the matched BPS sector weight converts the normalized response into the leading finite-radius two-source coefficient.

papers.title: A quantitative Robin Pólya--Szegő theorem for tangential polygons
papers.abstract: We extend the quantitative Dirichlet theorem of Gui, Hu, and Li \cite{GuiHuLi2026} to Robin torsional rigidity. For every fixed $β>0$, we prove that the regular $N$-gon uniquely maximizes Robin torsional rigidity among tangential $N$-gons of prescribed area. Our explicit perimeter deficit bound contains the Dirichlet deficit obtained by Gui, Hu, and Li \cite{GuiHuLi2026} and an additional Robin term that is positive for nonregular tangential polygons. For triangles, we answer the fixed-area optimization problem recorded as open by Keady and Wiwatanapataphee \cite[Appendix A.1.2]{KeadyWiwatanapataphee2016}. We also establish strict monotonicity along equal-area regular polygons as the number of sides increases, with an explicit bound for each consecutive gap. The proof combines mixed Robin--Neumann triangular cells, spectral estimates for angular concavity, and a quantitative scaling estimate.

papers.title: Ordinary lines, point degrees, and matroid density
papers.abstract: For every set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{C}^d$ with full affine span, we prove that some point lies on at least $n+1-2n/(d+1)$ spanned lines, which is best possible in every dimension. By successive contraction, this implies the sharp bound $r+(\ell-3)\binom r2$ on the number of elements of a simple rank-$r$ complex-representable matroid excluding $U_{2,\ell}$ as a minor, which removes the sufficiently-large-rank assumption from the bound of Geelen, Nelson, and Walsh. An arithmetic application shows that rank-$r$ integer matrices whose maximal minors have absolute value at most $Δ$ have at most $O(Δr^2)$ distinct columns, resolving a question of Averkov and Schymura. We prove that a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{C}^3$ determines at least $n^2/40$ ordinary lines whenever no plane contains more than $2n/3$ of the points. This answers a question of Basit, Dvir, Saraf, and Wolf. We also prove upper bounds on average line length and lower bounds on the number of points incident to many spanned lines in high-dimensional point sets. The proofs combine contraction of concentrated flats with normalization of the point vectors and second- and fourth-moment estimates on their pairwise correlations. This approach builds on the design matrix method.

papers.title: Half-space last passage percolation with inhomogeneous first row
papers.abstract: We consider exponential last passage percolation in half-space with a deterministic first row. This model corresponds to a version of TASEP in half-space in which particles enter at the origin and are restricted by a moving wall. We determine the possible limiting distributions of rescaled last passage times depending on the boundary strength and the choice of the wall. As key inputs to our analysis, we establish several results for point-to-point half-space last passage times, including upper tail bounds, weak convergence, and bounds on the probabilities that geodesics touch the diagonal for certain start and end points.

papers.title: Parallel Repetition for Entangled Games via Conditional Relative Entropy
papers.abstract: We give a proof of the cubic parallel-repetition bound for finite two-player entangled games using quantum conditional relative entropy. For a game with entangled value $1-\varepsilon<1$ and answer alphabets $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$, its $n$-fold repeated value is at most \[ \exp[-Ω(\varepsilon^3n/L)],\qquad L:=\max\{1,\log(|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|)\}, \] for every $n\ge1$. This recovers Song's cubic rate. We also prove a threshold bound: the probability of winning a fraction at least $1-\varepsilon+δ$ is at most $\exp[-Ω(δ^5n/(\varepsilon^2L))]$ for $0<δ\le\varepsilon$. Our information charge is the decrease in relative entropy when a question reference is discarded. Our comparison states preserve the original conditional question law. A chain rule bounds the coordinate charges using the cost of conditioning on checked wins and retaining checked answers. Our main lemma converts small charges into nearby pure-state descriptions and local corrections, each depending only on one player's question. Together with Song's sampler, these enable approximate local preparation of the conditioned workspace.

papers.title: Napoleonic triangles on the sphere from similar chord triangles
papers.abstract: We study a variant of Napoleon's construction on the unit sphere, in which the triangles erected on the sides of a spherical triangle $ABC$ are required to have similar isosceles chord triangles with apex angle $β\in(0,π/2)$. For a non-equilateral $ABC$, we prove that the triangle $XYZ$ of spherical circumcentres is equilateral if and only if $\cos(θ_a+θ_b+θ_c\pmΩ/2)=0$, where $θ_a,θ_b,θ_c$ are the base angles of the isosceles spherical triangles $XBC$, $YCA$, $ZAB$, $Ω$ is the area of $ABC$, and the sign $+$ (resp.~$-$) corresponds to the outward (resp.~inward) construction. We derive from this an explicit classification in terms of two quadrics and a cubic inequality. It recovers the theorem of Dipierro, Noakes and Valdinoci for $β=π/3$, and exhibits three families of solutions for $β>π/3$, together with a fourth one when $\cosβ<1/4$.

papers.title: Turing bifurcation, criticality, and multistability in a nonlocal advection-reaction-diffusion equation
papers.abstract: This paper considers a nonlocal advection--reaction--diffusion equation with logistic growth. We investigate how the interaction kernel affects the criticality of Turing bifurcations and the associated multistability. We first prove that nonhomogeneous stationary solutions bifurcate from the positive homogeneous stationary solution. Center manifold reduction yields an amplitude equation near the bifurcation point. This equation provides criteria for supercritical and subcritical bifurcations in terms of the Fourier transform of the interaction kernel. We also derive a sufficient condition for subcriticality. This condition can be satisfied by sufficiently localized attractive interactions. Based on these analytical results, we investigate multistability through numerical bifurcation analysis. The numerical results show that the stable homogeneous stationary solution can coexist with stable nonhomogeneous stationary solutions or stable time-periodic solutions.

papers.title: Small time asymptotics for kinetic SDEs with singular drift
papers.abstract: We study small-time asymptotics for kinetic stochastic differential equations with singular drifts in kinetic Kato classes. We establish a small-time large deviation principle and prove a pointwise Varadhan-type asymptotic for the associated transition density.

papers.title: When do quantum views help? Complementary classical-quantum representations in multi-view fusion
papers.abstract: Recent studies have reported promising results from quantum machine learning in drug discovery, healthcare, materials science and cybersecurity. Research includes comparisons with classical machine learning algorithms and the development of sequential hybrid pipelines. We propose that fusion can improve prediction when classical and quantum representations capture complementary predictive relationships. Our classical-quantum multi-view framework preserves the full classical input alongside simulated quantum features. Concatenation and attention combine the views; single-view comparisons, replacement and masking controls assess both views' contributions. Controlled angular-polynomial experiments distinguish targets adequately represented by a single view from those that depend on complementary angular and polynomial relationships. For these mixed targets, fusion improves prediction by combining the relevant feature sets, while matched classical representations recover the same benefit, linking the improvement to their complementary predictive content. Controlled classification tests further show that gains depend on alignment between the chosen representation and the target, and on a suitable fusion rule. Benchmark validation shows improved mean predictive performance over classical baselines on Wine, Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer, three-class Fashion-MNIST and Steel Plates Faults within the evaluated protocols. Classical replacement and masking controls remain competitive, classical baselines lead on Digits and Covertype, and outcomes with missing or corrupted views depend on the available inputs. These findings support evaluating quantum representations for their complementary predictive contribution and matching the representation and fusion strategy to the target relationships.

papers.title: Stronger Spectral Bound for Clique Number
papers.abstract: Given an integer $k$, deciding whether a graph has a clique of size $k$ is an NP-complete problem. Wilf's inequality provides a spectral lower bound for the clique number of a graph. Strengthening this bound, Elphick and Wocjan proposed a conjecture in 2018 using positive adjacency eigenvalues. In this paper, we present an infinite family of graphs for which the Elphick and Wocjan conjecture is true. We find a stronger spectral lower bound for the clique number for this family of graphs.

papers.title: Optimization of a Perturbed Implicit Sweeping Process by Constrained Discontinuous Controls
papers.abstract: This paper studies optimal control problems governed by an implicit sweeping process with velocity-dependent constraint geometry, where the dynamics are described by a differential inclusion involving the normal cone to a moving convex polyhedral set. Such systems form a challenging class of nonsmooth differential inclusions due to the implicit coupling between the state, velocity, and constraint reaction. To address these difficulties, we use a method of discrete approximations together with tools of variational analysis and generalized differentiation. This approach allows us to derive necessary optimality conditions for local minimizer in discrete-time problems and subsequently pass to the limit to obtain optimality conditions for the original continuous-time system. The obtained results extend existing optimal control theory for sweeping processes to a class of implicit dynamical systems with state-and velocity-dependent constraints.

papers.title: Optimally large cuts in both directions
papers.abstract: We prove that for every integer $d\ge2$ and all sufficiently large $m$, every digraph with $m$ edges and minimum outdegree at least $d$ has a vertex bipartition for which each directed cut is of size at least \[\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{2(2d-1)}m+\frac{d^2}{2(2d-1)}\right\rceil.\] The bound is sharp for infinitely many $m$. This answers for large graphs a question of Scott and proves a conjecture of Lee, Loh, and Sudakov. For $d=2$ we prove that $\lceil m/6\rceil$ is achievable for all $m$. We also establish a stability result characterizing near-extremal graphs.

papers.title: Observability as a constraint qualification for a nonsmooth bilevel PDE-constrained problem
papers.abstract: Motivated by experiment design for parameter identification in image reconstruction, we analyze a bilevel control problem involving sparse inversion at the lower level. Qualified optimality conditions in explicit multiplier form are shown to hold under either an observability condition for a coupled system or the Lebesgue nullity of a contact set induced by the lower-level adjoint variable. We prove that these conditions are independent of one another and that they cannot, in general, both be omitted. The approach is based on the characterization of local first-order geometric objects (tangent and normal cones) associated with a set of lifted constraints. Based on the resulting optimality conditions, we formulate a reduced gradient method and illustrate it through numerical experiments.

papers.title: Anti-successors and anti-replicators, Manin products and Koszul duality
papers.abstract: We develop an operadic theory of anti-splitting and anti-replication for binary operads. For a binary operad $\opd$, we define its anti-bisuccessor $\ABSu(\opd)$ and anti-trisuccessor $\ATSu(\opd)$, with the property that an operation of $\opd$ splits into a negative sum of two or three operations, yielding canonical operad morphisms $\opd \to\ABSu(\opd)$ and $\opd\to\ATSu(\opd)$. For binary quadratic operads, the process gives Manin black products, \[ \ABSu(\opd) \cong \antiprelie \bullet \opd, \qquad \ATSu(\opd)\cong \antipostlie\bullet\opd. \] Dually, we introduce the anti-duplicator \(\ADup(\mathcal P)\) and anti-triplicator \(\ATrip(\mathcal P)\) and prove \[ \ADup(\opd^!)\cong \ABSu(\opd)^!, \qquad \ATrip(\opd^!)\cong \ATSu(\opd)^!. \] Consequently, the anti-duplicator gives a new way to calculate Manin white products. %, in particular, $\ADup(\opd)\cong \antiperm\circ\opd$. The framework recovers known anti-splittings, including anti-dendriform, anti-pre-Lie, and anti-pre-Poisson structures, in a uniform operadic form and produces further examples and dual pairs.

papers.title: Two Sample Sizes in Test-Time LLM Ensembling: Buffered ERM and Minimax Theory
papers.abstract: Test-time scaling can improve the performance of large language models by generating multiple answers to a question and aggregating them. Weighted ensembles extend this idea by drawing answers from several models, with the weights determining how often each model is used. Learning these weights from a training dataset involves two sample sizes: $Q$ labeled questions and $N$ generations per model and question. We study their interplay through the clean risk, the population error of the ensemble's infinite-generation voting rule. Under a margin condition with exponent $β$, we show that empirical risk minimization (ERM) with a calibrated margin buffer achieves excess risk of order $Q^{-1/2}+N^{-β/2}$, up to logarithmic factors, for fixed numbers of models and candidate answers. To investigate the optimality of this dependence on $Q$ and $N$, we analyze a simplified submodel with two models and two possible answers per question. We characterize its minimax excess risk up to constants by a Hellinger modulus for a binomial-mixture experiment. Polynomial approximation and spectral analysis reveal three regimes. When questions are relatively scarce, the $Q^{-1/2}$ term governs learning and the general buffered ERM is optimal. In an intermediate regime, pooling generation counts across questions improves upon estimating each answer distribution separately, with only logarithmic gains from additional questions. With sufficiently many questions, the minimax excess risk reaches an $N^{-β}$ identification floor that persists even with infinitely many questions. The submodel's lower bounds also apply to general ensembles, matching the buffered-ERM upper bound up to logarithmic factors when questions are scarce and in parts of the intermediate regime. Questions remain about the transitions between regimes and the construction of matching pooled estimators for general ensembles.

papers.title: Fundamental Groups and Coregularity: Klt Pairs with Trivial and Nef Log-Anticanonical Class
papers.abstract: In this article, we study how the absolute coregularity of a projective log pair reflects on its fundamental group. More precisely, we show that for a projective klt log pair $(X,D)$ of absolute coregularity $c$ and arbitrary dimension the fundamental group $π_1^{\rm reg}(X,D)$ admits a normal abelian subgroup of finite index and rank at most $2c$. We reduce this statement to klt Calabi-Yau pairs with standard coefficients of dimension $c$. In the cases $0\le c\le2$ and fixed dimension, we can furthermore bound the index of a solvable normal subgroup. Combining the reduction with the recent regular-locus theorem of Fu-Guo-Song-Wang, we prove the coregularity bound in every dimension. In particular, for a projective klt pair $(X,D)$ with $-(K_X+D)$ nef, the orbifold fundamental group of the smooth locus is virtually abelian of rank at most $2\, {\rm dim}X$.

papers.title: Stitched surface codes: planar concatenation through GHZ corridors
papers.abstract: We present a fault-tolerant quantum-memory architecture that concatenates four distance-t rotated surface-code patches with the [[4,2,2]] outer code, encoding two logical qubits at code distance d = 2t in a physical footprint of N < 2(2t+1)^2 qubits on a square lattice with nearest-neighbor connectivity. The outer-code stabilizer generators XXXX and ZZZZ, each of physical weight 4t, are measured in situ via verified Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) ancillae distributed through narrow corridors between adjacent patches, without lattice surgery or long-range gates. The outer-code gadgets introduce hyperedge fault mechanisms, but by design each decomposes into graphlike components, so the complete syndrome is decoded by a single minimum-weight-perfect-matching pass. Circuit-level simulations show logical error rates that scale as p^t, consistent with distance-2t protection. Finally, we implement the construction experimentally on a 105-qubit Willow superconducting processor in both the ZZ and XX memory bases. With the correlated-matching decoder, increasing the code distance from d = 4 to d = 6 reduces the block logical error rate by a factor of 1.52. The construction thus provides a near-term testbed for concatenated architectures beyond the standard surface code.

papers.title: Dual Representations and Proxy Characterization of $H_2$ Norm for Partial Integral Equations
papers.abstract: Duality and dual representations are essential tools for systems theory and controller synthesis. For any finite-dimensional causal linear time-invariant (CLTI) system, there exists a dual CLTI system with identical $H_\infty$ and $H_2$ norm. These relations are found by simply taking the adjoint of the transfer function. For nonlinear, time-varying or infinite-dimensional systems, however, such a transfer function may not exist or be difficult to obtain. For duality in the $H_\infty$ norm, this obstacle is overcome by using the equivalent time-domain, induced $L_2$-norm characterization. For $H_2$ norms there is no such equivalent characterization and hence proxy norms such as induced energy to peak and impulse to energy norms are used. These proxy norms bound the $H_2$ norm in the CLTI case. However, neither of these $H_2$ proxy norms equal the same $H_2$ proxy of the canonical dual representation. In this paper, we overcome this by proposing a dual representation whose induced energy to peak proxy equals the impulse to energy proxy of the primal and vice-versa. This relation is developed in the context of Partial Integral Equation (PIE) representations. The result is then used to establish primal-dual operator inequalities for both proxy norms similar in form to the primal-dual LMIs used to characterize the $H_2$ norm.

papers.title: Honesty is the Best Policy ... or is it? Demand Management for Probabilistic Service Options
papers.abstract: To enable well-informed customer choices and redistribute demand across service options, providers can display probabilities regarding predicted service levels at the time of booking, effectively offering probabilistic service options. In many service settings, the underlying truthful probabilities endogenously depend on the system state, rather than being static product attributes controlled by the provider. While customers rely on this information when making decisions, they cannot readily verify its accuracy. Consequently, providers may be tempted to manipulate the displayed probabilities to guide customers' choices in their favor, creating a novel lever for demand management. In this work, we model the resulting problem as a sequential decision process, define truthful probabilities recursively, and introduce transparency constraints that limit their distortion. Because the exact computation of truthful probabilities is intractable for realistic settings, we develop an adapted reinforcement learning algorithm to approximate them. Furthermore, we propose a sampling-based mixed-integer program to optimize the information communicated by the provider in each state. Our framework enables providers to gauge the benefits of dynamically disclosing probabilistic information at the time of booking and sheds light on incentives for manipulation. Our computational study is motivated by out-of-home delivery, i.e., the delivery to parcel lockers or shops, and reveals a trade-off between individual-level transparency and aggregate customer utilities.

papers.title: Functions of bounded variation are not dense in the Strong BD Norm
papers.abstract: We prove that functions of bounded variation are not dense in the space of functions of bounded deformation with respect to the strong BD norm. Using alternating Riesz products and directional slicing, we construct on every nonempty open subset of $\R^n$ ($n\ge2$) a continuous, compactly supported BD function that is at positive distance from BV.

papers.title: Matrix Completion Discriminants
papers.abstract: We introduce the matrix completion discriminant of a graph as the Zariski closure of the set of partial symmetric matrices whose completion fibers fail to meet a rank stratum transversely. A clique-sum formula for the matrix completion discriminant is established for arbitrary graphs, while explicit defining equations for cycles are obtained in terms of iterated resultants. Using these results together with the analysis of $K_4$-minor-free graphs, we prove that for every cycle-completable graph, the discriminant factors into determinant factors from maximal cliques and resultant factors from chordless cycles.

papers.title: Dimension-Free PAC-Bayes Generalization for Deep Neural Networks via Dirichlet Processes
papers.abstract: Classical PAC-Bayesian generalization theory places prior distributions over Euclidean parameter space $Θ\subseteq \mathbb{R}^D$, causing relative entropy to scale with network dimension $D$. For modern overparameterized neural networks where $D \gg n$, this parameter-counting dependency yields vacuous generalization bounds ($> 1{,}000\%$). In this work, we resolve this barrier by shifting prior specification from internal parameters to the non-parametric space of data distributions $\mathcal{M}_1(\mathcal{Z})$ via a \textbf{Dirichlet Process (DP)}, $\mathcal{DP}(α, F_0)$, inducing parameter distributions through push-forward measures under the learning algorithm. By the Data Processing Inequality, parameter-space relative entropy is strictly bounded by the data-space DP divergence, which we evaluate in exact closed form using Digamma functions. The resulting PAC-Bayesian certificate is strictly invariant to network parameter count $D$, width, and depth. On intrinsic $d^*$-dimensional submanifolds, optimal partition scaling achieves the minimax non-parametric rate $\mathcal{O}(n^{-1/(d^*+2)} \sqrt{\ln n})$. Across vision architectures scaling up to 4.2 million parameters ($D = 7{,}850$ to $D = 4{,}203{,}522$) on the full MNIST benchmark, while classical weight-space bounds scale past $940\%$ (becoming vacuous), our data-space DP-PAC-Bayes certificate remains stable, non-vacuous, and certified at \textbf{$8.8\%$--$9.4\%$}.

papers.title: Higher-order necessary conditions for nonscattering
papers.abstract: We study the scattering of incident waves by a class of planar analytic inhomogeneities with constant refractive index, governed by the Helmholtz equation. We derive an infinite hierarchy of necessary conditions for nonscattering: any complex analytic nonscattering incident wave must satisfy infinitely many differential constraints at a specific point determined by the geometry of the inhomogeneity. As an application, we show that for any noncircular elliptical inhomogeneity, every single separated (Mathieu) mode necessarily scatters. This is in stark contrast to the circular case, where single separated (Bessel) modes are nonscattering at infinitely many wavenumbers.

papers.title: Directional delays and singular strong-barrier limits for Fisher--KPP propagation across a semipermeable interface
papers.abstract: We study Fisher--KPP propagation from compactly supported data across a planar semipermeable interface in $N\ge2$ dimensions, with unit diffusion and $f'(0)=1$. For every finite resistance, the receiving front has speed $2$ and logarithmic correction $-(N+2)\log t/2$. Its phase is determined by a positive directional amplitude on the closed receiving hemisphere. This amplitude is jointly continuous in resistance and direction and is Hölder continuous in direction with exponent $1/3$. It also determines a threshold-independent signed arrival-time difference. Under concavity, the amplitude decreases strictly with resistance. As the resistance $β$ tends to infinity, the amplitude is asymptotic to $2(4π)^{-N/2}I_N(θ)(\logβ)/β$ uniformly on each fixed receiving cone bounded away from the equator. Here $I_N$ is a weighted input moment of the closed Neumann donor problem. Although this moment diverges logarithmically near the equator, the equatorial amplitude tends to half the amplitude of the even Neumann donor solution. The strong-resistance and equatorial limits therefore do not commute. The proof combines critical derivative moments, an integrated Robin trace estimate, Cartesian leading-edge limits, and matching through the wave displacement. The phase and asymptotic formulas require only the smooth KPP assumptions, without the additional restriction $f'\le f'(0)$. Concavity is used for strict resistance ordering and the strict bounds on the limiting equatorial delay.

papers.title: Critical Ising Model on the Periodic Cubic Lattice $(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^{3}$
papers.abstract: We investigate the critical behaviour of the nearest-neighbour Ising model on the three-dimensional periodic cubic lattice $(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^{3}$, and we present a companion set of Monte Carlo simulations.
