Second, we derive a convex dual representation that extends weak Kantorovich duality and stochastic optimal transport duality to controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics. Finally, for the mean field Schrödinger problem, we prove convergence, at the level of value functions, of the associated finite-particle Schrödinger bridge problems to the mean field limit, thereby identifying the nonlinear problem as the exact infinite-particle limit of finite-particle Schrödinger bridges. As a byproduct, we establish the existence of an optimal mean field Schrödinger potential, providing a variational foundation for duality in nonlinear stochastic transport.

papers.title: From Syndromes to Computation: A General Framework for Logical Operations in Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires error-correcting codes that not only protect quantum information but also support useful logical operations with practical physical realizations. Here we develop a general framework in which the stabilizer syndromes of commuting Pauli rotations directly organize logical-gate design. We derive an exact codespace-preservation condition valid at arbitrary rotation angles, providing a common stabilizer-level description for CSS and non-CSS codes and for both Clifford and non-Clifford operations. A particularly useful equal-syndrome specialization reduces Clifford gate design to stabilizer factorization, yields a general generator weight bound of $\lceil d/2\rceil$ for distance-$d$ codes, and systematically extends to logical rotations higher in the Clifford hierarchy. Applied to bivariate-bicycle (BB) and non-CSS Mirror qLDPC codes, the framework gives explicit low-weight Clifford and controlled-phase gates. Our implementations yield new low-weight gates, including an addressed $T$ gate on the $[[16,4,4]]$ BB code, $T$-type rotations on the $[[64,8,8]]$ BB code, and CCZ-, CS-, and $T$-type operations on the $[[36,6,6]]$ Mirror code. We also develop analytic constructions using Clifford algebra bases, which turn the syndrome constraints into explicit algebraic relations and provide a systematic route to logical addressability. We use this approach to analytically construct addressed CNOT, SWAP, controlled, and CCZ-type gates on recursive hypercube codes. An independent construction on middle quantum Reed--Muller codes yields C${}^r$Z gates that saturate the equal-syndrome weight bound. These results establish stabilizer syndromes as a constructive link between the stabilizer structure of a quantum code, the logical computations it can directly support, and the fault-tolerance properties of their physical realizations.

papers.title: $3$-manifold groups are linear
papers.abstract: We prove that the fundamental group of every compact graph $3$-manifold is linear over the complex numbers. As a corollary, all fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are linear over the complex numbers.

papers.title: Stability Transfer for Autonomous Systems via Higher-Order Taylor-Truncated Lyapunov Certificates
papers.abstract: We develop analytical sufficient conditions for certifying the local asymptotic stability of nonlinear autonomous systems based on Lyapunov functions derived from their finite-order Taylor polynomial approximations. This approach translates the stability analysis problem from the original nonlinear dynamics to a more computationally tractable polynomial domain. The derived conditions allow for the explicit calculation of a guaranteed inner approximation of the region of attraction ($\mathrm{ROA}$). We show how sum-of-squares (SOS) programming and grid search can be used to systematically search for polynomial Lyapunov functions that yield a large certified threshold radius and extract a certified invariant set inner approximation of the $\mathrm{ROA}$ of the nonpolynomial original system. The framework is then applied to a control tuning problem: finding reduced-effort Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) controllers that ensure that a given initial state of interest belongs to the certified $\mathrm{ROA}$ of the nonpolynomial closed loop system. The effectiveness of the overall methodology is demonstrated using a pendulum with nonlinear damping and a nonlinear control system.

papers.title: Clean handshake sequences
papers.abstract: After a basketball game, each of the $n$ players on Team A must shake hands with each of the $n$ players on Team B. What is the minimum number of (reversible, ambidextrous) gloves required so that zero germ transmission occurs? We show that the answer is $3n/2+o(n)$ and develop a general theory for prescribed handshake sets.

papers.title: Existence of positive solutions to anisotropic elliptic equations in the entire Euclidean space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we research an anisotropic elliptic equation in the entire Euclidean space R^{N} . Under the assumption that the nonlinearity of the equation has exponential or critical growth, we prove, by means of the mountain-pass theorem, that the equation admits a nontrivial positive weak solution. Moreover, applying the mountain-pass theorem and Ekeland's variational principle, we show that a perturbation of the equation possesses two distinct positive weak solutions.

papers.title: Strong convergence rate of the implicit midpoint method for stochastic KdV equations
papers.abstract: We establish a strong convergence rate for the implicit midpoint method applied to the periodic stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equation with additive noise, addressing a question that has remained open since the work of Debussche and Printems. To control nonlinear error growth, we obtain exponential integrability estimates for the exact and comparison solutions using the coercivity of a classical KdV invariant. We then derive local error bounds from estimates for the comparison solutions and control error accumulation through an $L^2$ error propagation identity that isolates a martingale increment. Under $H_0^{9/2}$ regularity assumptions on the noise and the deterministic initial data, we prove that, on every fixed finite time interval, the maximum $L^2(\mathbb{T})$ error at the time points is $O(h)$ in $L^p(Ω)$ for every $1\le p<\infty$. Notably, the exponential integrability and the convergence rate hold for every damping coefficient $λ\ge0$, including the undamped case $λ=0$. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted first-order convergence.

papers.title: Fast charging of quantum batteries assisted by nonlinear couplings
papers.abstract: Charger-mediated quantum batteries offer promising opportunities for efficient energy transfer and storage at the quantum level, with potential advantages beyond their classical counterparts. Here, we theoretically demonstrate that nonlinear charger-battery interactions can substantially accelerate the charging of quantum batteries. In the weak-driving regime, sufficiently strong nonlinear coupling can dominate over the effect of dephasing and significantly reduce the charging time. In the strong- and optimal-driving regimes, where the optimal driving strength maximizes the steady-state ergotropy in the linear-coupling regime, nonlinear coupling gives rise to a new optimum in the charging time beyond that of the linear-coupling regime, accompanied by nearly critically damped dynamics. Remarkably, even in the absence of external driving, nonlinear coupling alone can substantially reduce the charging time, providing an alternative route toward fast battery charging. Our results establish nonlinear charger-battery coupling as an effective resource for accelerating quantum-battery charging and broaden the scope of interaction-enabled quantum advantages in energy transfer and storage.

papers.title: On extending induced subgraphs
papers.abstract: When characterizing graphs defined by forbidden induced subgraphs, it is often desirable to understand how a graph $G$ can be generated incrementally from a given induced subgraph $H$. In this paper, we study a number of problems within this framework. First, for several notions of connectivity, we determine all minimal induced subgraphs of $G$ that contain $H$ and attain the connectivity of $G$. Second, we establish how to grow $H$ inside $G$ while preserving twin-freeness and certain forms of connectivity. Third, we establish {\it finite test theorems} for various graph classes, proving that agreement with the recursively generated graphs for a few initial iterations forces agreement at all subsequent iterations. Consequently, such an infinite graph family can be completely determined by finitely many of its initial generations. As an application, we characterize $\{\mathbb L_1,\mathbb L_3\}$-free graphs, where $\mathbb L_1$ is the claw and $\mathbb L_3$ is another forbidden graph for line graphs. Our structural results reduce this problem to a finite verification, which is completed through computer-assisted computation.

papers.title: Roth's theorem on weighted projective lines
papers.abstract: Let ${\mathbb P}^1_{\mathfrak q}$ be the weighted projective line with coprime weights ${\mathfrak q}=(q_0,q_1)$ and $L=q_0q_1$. The weighted Veronese map $Φ\colon {\mathbb P}^1_{\mathfrak q}\to {\mathbb P}^1$ satisfies $h\circΦ=L\,{\mathfrak s}$. Pulling back Roth's theorem gives the optimal exponent $2L$ for the full rational orbit set. For points represented by coprime integral coordinates, counting suggests the smaller exponent $q_0+q_1$. We formulate this as a conjecture and prove an $S$-adic radical form under the $abc$ conjecture. For ${\mathfrak q}=(2,3)$ the resulting inequality at the target $[1:1]$ is the coprime Hall-type inequality, and Danilov--Elkies examples show that the exponent $5$ is sharp. We also prove the expected exponent unconditionally over characteristic-zero function fields for constant targets and polynomial approximants, and for almost every real target. A weighted $abc$ formulation is introduced; in signature $(3,2)$ finitely many coefficient pairs are equivalent to $abc$, and weighted Belyi maps transfer this input to arbitrary algebraic targets. Applications include a pullback form of Schmidt's subspace theorem, weighted Thue inequalities, and a counterexample to a naive weighted rescaling of Roth's index construction.

papers.title: Global existence of large strong solutions to the 3D compressible micropolar equations with density-dependent viscosities
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem for the three-dimensional (3D) compressible micropolar equations with density-dependent viscosities. By classical $L^p$ estimates to elliptic system, defining suitable energy functions, after the elaborate index analysis, we establish the global existence of strong solutions to the system with all viscosities depending density as long as the initial density is large enough. By product, We also prove the existence of global large strong solutions with only large initial shear viscosity $μ_1(ρ)$ and angular viscosity $μ_2(ρ)$, which consists with the research work \cite{ZZ2014} of 3D compressible Navier-Stokes equations with constant viscosities and improve the recent result of \cite{HLZ} in some extent where they requiring both initial shear viscosity and bulk viscosity to be large.

papers.title: Nonhomogeneous Subordinators and Lévy Copulas for Reliability Analysis of Time-Dependent Degradation Processes
papers.abstract: Many systems in engineering applications may experience complex multi-dimensional degradation processes involving random jumps. Analyzing the reliability of such degradation processes presents significant challenges. Previously developed models have utilized multi-dimensional Lévy subordinators and Lévy copulas to describe these processes, with reliability functions expressed through characteristic functions and Laplace transforms (Shu et al., 2015, 2016, Shi et al., 2020, Shi and Feng, 2024). However, these models are restricted to stationary linear paths and homogeneous Lévy subordinators. In real-world scenarios, increments in a degradation process are often time-dependent and nonhomogeneous. To address this limitation of previous studies, this work extends existing degradation models by introducing nonhomogeneous Lévy subordinators, which are designed to capture time-varying complexities inherent in degradation processes. Unlike conventional degradation models that often assume a constant rate of jumps, nonhomogeneous Lévy subordinators aim to provide a more flexible representation of degradation behaviors that evolve under varying external conditions and internal system dynamics. Additionally, the joint behaviors of multiple degradation processes are characterized using Lévy copulas, enabling a more comprehensive analysis of system reliability. Numerical examples are provided to illustrate the applicability of these models in lifetime analysis.

papers.title: Risk-Averse Inference-Time Diffusion Model Alignment with Finite-Sample Guarantees
papers.abstract: Inference-time alignment steers diffusion models toward downstream objectives without costly fine-tuning, but existing methods typically optimize expected cost (or reward) without explicitly controlling tail risk. In this work, we propose a risk-averse framework for inference-time alignment of diffusion models that balances expected cost and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) under trajectory-level Kullback-Leibler regularization. We characterize the optimal path distribution and reverse transitions as functions of the CVaR threshold, reducing the alignment problem to a one-dimensional optimization problem over the threshold. We show that this one-dimensional optimization problem can be nonconvex in general, establish sufficient conditions for convexity, and introduce quadratic regularization to enable efficient derivative-free ternary search. Under suitable assumptions, we provide finite-sample guarantees for threshold optimization and value estimation, and combine them into a terminal total-variation bound relative to the regularized target under exact resampling. Experiments on synthetic data and image generation using Stable Diffusion demonstrate improved tail performance over risk-neutral baselines while maintaining competitive average cost.

papers.title: On the existence problem for a double mean field equation and its application to prescribed curvature problems
papers.abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a compact Riemann surface with smooth boundary $\partial M$. Let $K(x)>0$, $h(x)> 0$ or $h(x)\equiv 0$ be two smooth functions on $M$ and $\partial M$ respectively. In this paper, we consider the following double mean field type equation with a nonlinear Neumann boundary condition related to a prescribed curvature problem \begin{equation}\label{equation:01} \begin{cases} \displaystyle -Δ_g u+\frac{4π}{|M|} =2ρ\frac{Ke^u}{\int_MKe^u\,dv_g}, & \text{in }M,\\[1.2em] \displaystyle \partial_νu =2ρ'\frac{he^{u/2}}{\int_{\partial M}he^{u/2}\,ds_g}, & \text{on }\partial M, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $ρ> 0,\ ρ'\geq 0$ and $ρ+ρ'=2π$, $ν$ is the outward unit normal vector to $\partial M$. When $h\equiv 0$, the second equation changes to $\partial_νu=0$ on $\partial M$. By introducing a boundary integration constant, we obtain a sufficient condition under which \eqref{equation:01} admits a solution. As a geometric application, we solve the prescribed curvature equation for both the Gauss curvature and the geodesic curvature in the case that $M$ is topologically a disk. When $(M,g)$ is the standard hemisphere $\mathbb S^2_+$, let $p\in \partial \mathbb S^2_+$ be a maximum point of $$ Φ(q)=h(q)+\sqrt{h(q)^2+K(q)}, \qquad q\in\partial \mathbb S^2_+. $$ Suppose \begin{equation*} K_ν(p)+2Φ(p)(-Δ_{\partial \mathbb S^2_+})^{1/2}h(p)<0. \end{equation*} Then the prescribed curvature problem \begin{align*} -Δ_g u+\frac{4π}{|M|}=2Ke^u, \text{in }\mathbb S^2_+,\ \ \partial_νu=2he^{u/2}, \text{on }\partial \mathbb S^2_+. \end{align*} admits a smooth solution.

papers.title: An $\eps$-regularity criterion at one scale for 3-D Navier-Stokes equations and improved upper bound on the box dimension of the interior singular set
papers.abstract: In this paper, we obtain an $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion at one scale for 3D Navier-Stokes equations using a coarse-to-refined estimate argument based on mean-fluctuation decomposition. Making use of this $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion, we improve the upper bound on the box dimension of the interior singular set to $15/13$.

papers.title: A Structure-Preserving Effective Linear Approximation of the Quantum Boltzmann Collision Operator
papers.abstract: We construct a structure-preserving effective linear approximation of the quantum Boltzmann collision operator for Bose and Fermi gases in the normal phase. For variable hard-sphere kernels, the resulting Fourier spectral evaluation costs $O(N_v^4\log N_v)$, with $N_v$ velocity nodes per direction and no angular quadrature factor. The continuous operator conserves mass, momentum and energy and satisfies a linearized $H$-theorem. We also use the operator at local quantum equilibrium as an approximate collision Jacobian in a modified Newton solver that retains the full nonlinear residual. Numerical tests show smaller errors than the quantum BGK model in homogeneous relaxation and fewer full collision evaluations for steady Couette and Fourier flows than the same Newton solver using a quantum BGK Jacobian.

papers.title: Targeted Entropy-Stable Nonlinear Artificial Dissipation for High-Order Spectral-Element Summation-By-Parts Discretizations
papers.abstract: Artificial dissipation improves the robustness of high-order methods for under-resolved flows, but can compromise accuracy and suppress physically relevant structures if its strength and spatial distribution are not appropriately controlled. We present a sensor-activated nonlinear artificial-dissipation framework, inspired by the residual correction method, for continuous and discontinuous summation-by-parts discretizations. In contrast to many existing spectral-element dissipation operators that either reduce the formal order of accuracy or target only the highest polynomial modes, the proposed framework permits design- and higher-order dissipation with explicit control over its magnitude, spatial distribution, activation, and convergence rate under mesh refinement. This modular construction also recovers several existing methods through appropriate choices of its components. The dissipation preserves discrete conservation and semidiscrete entropy stability whenever the base method satisfies these properties. It is dimensionally consistent, element local, and discretization agnostic, as the added term is constructed independently of the base spatial residual. For smooth solutions under suitable mesh assumptions, we establish parameter choices that retain the formal accuracy of the base discretization. Numerical experiments with summation-by-parts discretizations of the Burgers and Euler equations demonstrate substantially improved robustness for under-resolved flows and flows with shock waves while retaining high-order accuracy for smooth solutions, using the same parameter choices across several test problems. Overall, these results show that targeted dissipation can improve the robustness of high-order methods without excessive damping of resolved flow structures.

papers.title: On the Real Waring Rank of a Biharmonic Form
papers.abstract: We develop an effective method for determining the real Waring rank and the real border rank of biharmonic binary forms. By means of real apolarity, we convert both of these problems into membership questions for regions bounded by a hypocycloid and an epicycloid. We further provide a computable algebraic criterion for the relevant memberships, which involves only the signs of certain real-valued resultants.

papers.title: Boundary Control of a Modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest Beam via Reduced-Order Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the active vibration control of an elastic beam using reinforcement learning (RL). The physical system is modeled by a modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest type linear partial differential equation with simply supported boundary conditions. The dynamics are approximated by a reduced-order model (ROM) obtained through eigenvalue expansion and truncated Galerkin projection. Control is applied through boundary actuation. The resulting finite-dimensional system is formulated as a continuous-time Markov decision process and solved numerically using the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. All modeling steps, from physical formulation to temporal discretization and control design, are explicitly described. A systematic comparison is performed between the controller learned via PPO and the classical linear quadratic (LQR) regulator. The analysis highlights the strengths and limitations of each approach, both from a theoretical and practical point of view, with particular emphasis on energy dissipation mechanisms and actuator constraints.

papers.title: The $\ell$-degree Turán densities of hypergraphs: infinite families and their finite subfamilies
papers.abstract: Let $k>\ell\ge 1$ be integers. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-uniform hypergraphs ($k$-graphs), its $\ell$-degree Turán density $γ^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of the normalized minimum $\ell$-degree over all $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs. In this paper, we prove that for all integers $k>\ell>2$ and every $α\in[0,1)$, there exists an infinite family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs such that $γ^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F})=α$, while every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subset \mathcal{F}$ satisfies $γ^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F}')>α$. This confirms the conjecture of Mubayi and Zhao on codegree Turán densities for every $k > 3$. As an immediate consequence, the set $Γ^{k,\ell}_{\infty}$ of $\ell$-degree Turán densities of nonempty $k$-graph families is $[0,1)$ whenever $k>\ell>2$, which answers a question of Lo and Markström from 2014.

papers.title: Efficient Shallow Ritz Method: 1D Semi-Linear Diffusion-Reaction and Allen-Cahn Equations
papers.abstract: An efficient shallow Ritz method was developed in [8, 9] for one-dimensional linear diffusion and diffusion-reaction problems. In this paper, the method is extended to a nonlinear diffusion-reaction equation with a cubic reaction term: (1) a basic error estimate of the shallow Ritz discretization is established and (2) a reduced block Newton (rBN) method for solving the resulting non-convex optimization problem is developed. Again, the computational cost of the rBN method is $\mathcal{O}(n)$ for one-dimensional problems, where $n$ is the number of neurons. Combining a convex splitting scheme for time discretization with the efficient shallow Ritz method, we develop a time-stepping neural network method for solving the Allen-Cahn equation. The unconditional energy stability of the time discretization and an error estimate in the $L^2$ norm are established. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the neural network approach yields accurate solutions for singularly perturbed nonlinear diffusion-reaction equations and the Allen-Cahn equation. The method effectively resolves interior and boundary layers without oscillations and significantly outperforms the finite element method on fixed uniform meshes.

papers.title: On the generalized cospectral mates of chain graphs of rank 4
papers.abstract: A graph is called a chain graph if it is bipartite and the neighborhoods of the vertices in each color class are linearly ordered by inclusion. We study the generalized spectral determination of chain graphs of adjacency rank $4$. We first show that generalized cospectral chain graphs have the same number of isolated vertices, reducing the problem to the connected case. For connected rank-$4$ chain graphs, we derive four explicit equations in the cell parameters that are necessary and sufficient for generalized cospectrality. These equations reduce to a quadratic equation in a single parameter. As a consequence, every connected rank-$4$ chain graph has at most one generalized cospectral mate, and the possible mate can be reconstructed explicitly. We further obtain a simple sufficient condition for a rank-$4$ chain graph to be determined by its generalized spectrum (DGS) and, in particular, prove that every double star graph is DGS. Finally, we construct an explicit infinite family of non-double-star rank-$4$ chain graphs that are DGS but not determined by their adjacency spectra, with both the graphs and their complements being connected.

papers.title: Fragments of SRP, the nonstationary ideal, and diagonal reflection
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationships between fragments of SRP and diagonal reflection principles. It turns out that the subcomplete fragment of SRP, augmented with CH, implies that the nonstationary ideal on $ω_1$ is not saturated, but that Larson's diagonal reflection principle $OSR_{ω_2}$ holds. In contrast, it was known that the full principle SRP implies the saturation of the nonstationary ideal on $ω_1$, but it does not imply $OSR_{ω_2}$. We find several instances of this phenomenon: pairing (variations of) the subcomplete fragment of SRP with stronger failures of the nonstationary ideal on $ω_1$ to be saturated allows us to conclude more instances of diagonal reflection principles, while boosting (the corresponding variations of) the full principle SRP with strong forms of the saturation of the nonstationary ideal allows us to produce models where these principles still hold, yet weaker versions of diagonal reflection fail.

papers.title: Aperiodic automorphisms of the Razak--Jacelon algebra
papers.abstract: We completely classify aperiodic automorphisms of the Razak--Jacelon algebra $\mathcal{W}$ up to outer conjugacy. As a technical ingredient, based on the works of Connes, Herman--Ocneanu, Kishimoto, and Sato, we introduce a notion of weak stability for automorphisms of simple separable monotracial C$^*$-algebras. We also consider automorphisms of UHF algebras of infinite type and the Jiang--Su algebra. In particular, we classify aperiodic ``UHF-absorbing'' automorphisms of UHF algebras of infinite type up to outer conjugacy.

papers.title: Convex-Analytic View of Query Selection for Safety Verification of Markov Decision Processes
papers.abstract: Safety verification of a Markov decision process (MDP) asks whether the probabilities of reaching several failure states jointly lie in a convex safe region under every scheduler. Watanabe and Unno (2026) prove safety by refining an outer approximation of the failure probabilities, where each query bounds a nonnegative weighted sum of the probabilities. Their rule selects weights by the largest Euclidean violation. We present a unified framework to measure violation in an explicitly chosen error unit: directions are scored by the support-function gap between the outer approximation and the safe region, normalized by the support function of the unit. We show that the maximal score, when positive, equals the smallest enlargement of the safe region in multiples of that unit that contains the outer approximation. The Euclidean unit recovers the earlier rule; two new rules are generated by the unit cube and the safe region itself. We experimentally evaluate how the choice of measurement rule affects the performance of safety verification for MDPs.

papers.title: Sharp Damping Location for Stability of a Locally Damped Wave Equation and its Galerkin Approximation
papers.abstract: We study the stability of the variable coefficient wave equation $u_{tt}-u_{xx}-(1+x^{2})u_{yy}+χ_{\mathbb G}u_{t}=0$ on the rectangle $(-1,1)\times(0,π)$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions, where the viscous damping acts on a vertical strip $\mathbb G=(η-δ,η+δ)\times(0,π)$. We establish a precise relationship between the location of the damping region and the rate of energy decay. We prove that the associated semigroup is exponentially stable whenever the closure of the damping strip meets the line $x=0$, i.e., $|η|\leqδ$, despite the existence of rays that never enter the damped region. When the damping region is strictly bounded away from $x=0$, the semigroup decays at the sharp rate $(\log(2+t))^{-1}$. The proofs combine separation of variables, one-dimensional resolvent estimates, a reflection identity for the harmonic oscillator, and Gaussian quasimodes. We then consider the spectral Galerkin approximation based on the Dirichlet eigenfunctions of the constant coefficient Laplacian and show that, although the sequence of semigroups resulting from the approximation converges to the continuous one, it fails to be uniformly exponentially stable.

papers.title: On a finite group in which every non-supersolvable maximal subgroup is a TI-subgroup
papers.abstract: We provide a complete characterization of a finite group in which every non-supersolvable maximal subgroup is a TI-subgroup, which generalizes some known related results.

papers.title: Hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces
papers.abstract: We study hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces. We show that any number of general points on a $K3$ surface of Picard rank one can be connected by a hyperelliptic curve. As a by-product we recover the Beauville--Voisin decomposition of the small diagonal, together with some new bounds on its torsion order in the integral Chow group. On the arithmetic side, given a $K3$ surface $X$ of geometric Picard rank one defined over a number field $k$, we show that there exists a finite extension $k\subset k'$ such that quadratic points are dense in $X_{k'}$, extending a theorem of Corvaja--Zucconi to $K3$ surfaces of arbitrary degree.

papers.title: On horn-shaped Reinhardt domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of unbounded Reinhardt domains in $\mathbb C^n$ ($n\geq 2$),which we call horn domains. We study the dimensions of the Bergman spaces,the holomorphic sectional curvature of the Bergman metric, and the holomorphic equivalence problem for such horn Reinhardt domains.

papers.title: Monoidal structure on Rota-Baxter algebras via augmentation, and free cocycle bialgebras
papers.abstract: A tensor product is known for commutative Rota--Baxter algebras through a universal construction, but its underlying algebra need not be the ordinary tensor product $A\otimes B$ and can be substantially larger. We show that, after passing to augmented Rota--Baxter algebras, the ordinary tensor product itself carries a natural Rota--Baxter operator which makes the category monoidal with the usual associator and unit constraints. The resulting structure is intrinsically nonsymmetric: over a field of characteristic zero, this operator and its flip-conjugated counterpart are the only possibilities among linear combinations of five natural terms, while over any field the full category admits no braiding. Its comonoid objects are precisely Rota--Baxter cocycle bialgebras. Moreover, the free Rota--Baxter adjunction yields a bimonad and free cocycle bialgebras on ordinary bialgebras, with compatible Hopf structures for connected filtered inputs, in both the associative and commutative settings.

papers.title: Fractional Calderón problem with $L^{\infty}$-conductivities
papers.abstract: We study the inverse problem for the fractional conductivity equation with uniformly elliptic conductivities $γ\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$. For every $n\geq1$ and $0<s<1$, we prove that the local exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on any nonempty open subset of the exterior of a bounded open domain determines $γ$ uniquely almost everywhere in $\mathbb R^n$. No continuity, Sobolev regularity, or prescribed behavior at infinity is required. The proof works directly with the conductivity bilinear form and avoids the fractional Liouville reduction. It combines exterior determination at Lebesgue points, equality of weighted solutions, and a unique continuation principle for the fractional Laplacian in the weighted class \[ L_s=\left\{ g\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n): \int_{\mathbb R^n} \frac{|g(x)|}{1+|x|^{n+2s}}\,dx<\infty \right\}. \] Specifically, if $g\in L_s$ and both $g$ and $(-Δ)^s g$ vanish in a nonempty open set, with the latter equality understood distributionally, then $g=0$ almost everywhere. This result requires neither local boundedness nor Sobolev regularity of $g$. Its proof uses the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and boundary unique continuation for the associated degenerate elliptic equation.

papers.title: Schauder estimate in large scale for compressible planar cavity flows with fast-decaying vorticity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study planar compressible cavity flows fast-decaying vorticity and establish a Schauder estimate in large scale. As an application, we obtain an a priori asymptotic growth rate estimate of the cavity, that $s^{\frac{1}{2}-δ}\lesssim h(s)\lesssim s^{\frac{1}{2}+δ}$. This is by far the most accurate asymptotic estimate for compressible cavity flows and is probably the first paper that takes vorticity into account in the asymptotic analysis.

papers.title: Chromatic Block-Gibbs p-Bit Decoding of QLDPC Codes
papers.abstract: We introduce a parallel decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes based on probabilistic bits (p-bits), tunable stochastic binary units controlled by local fields. The idea is that predicted error configurations, interpreted as explanations of the observed syndrome, are updated stochastically using local Gibbs conditionals, while a progressively strengthened parity penalty drives the search toward syndrome-valid configurations. A coloring of the decoding graph enables parallel block updates, and independent replicas and restarts provide trajectory diversity. The best candidate encountered during the search is returned, mirroring the candidate-selection strategy of recent ensemble decoders. At the stated update budgets, the resulting logical error rates are on par with leading decoders under both code-capacity and circuit-level noise. While the total number of variable resamplings can be substantially larger than the message-update count of BP-based alternatives, the numerical results establish constraint-annealed p-bit dynamics as a competitive stochastic alternative for QLDPC decoding and motivate further study of hardware-native implementations.

papers.title: Recovery of Rough Sources in the Inverse Monge--Ampère Problem
papers.abstract: We prove that every nonnegative source \(f\in L^1(Ω)\) in the Monge--Ampère equation \[ \det D^2u=f\quad\text{in }Ω, \] on a bounded uniformly convex \(C^{1,1}\) domain \(Ω\subset\mathbb R^n\), \(n\geq2\), is uniquely determined by generalized boundary measurements of Alexandrov solutions. The measurement is the extremal boundary slope, which extends the outward normal derivative and may equal \(+\infty\). For each \(ω\in\mathbb S^{n-1}\), it suffices to know these slopes for the cylindrical Dirichlet data \[ \frac{t_k^ω}{2}|P_ωx|^2,\qquad t_k^ω\to\infty, \] along any sequence of amplitudes, where \(P_ω\) projects onto \(ω^\perp\). The boundary value and extremal slope determine the interior subgradient image up to a Lebesgue null set. An exact change-of-variables formula and a large-amplitude limit then recover the Euclidean X-ray transform of \(f\), yielding uniqueness without a positive lower bound on the source. For nonnegative \(L^\infty\) sources, the extremal slopes are bounded and coincide with the interior normal derivatives, giving a Dirichlet-to-interior-Neumann formulation. The argument also extends to \[ \vartheta(\nabla u)\det D^2u=f, \] where the known weight \(\vartheta\) is locally integrable, Borel measurable, and bounded below by a positive constant. Conditional on existence of the corresponding Alexandrov solutions, the same cylindrical boundary-slope data determine every nonnegative \(L^1\) source.

papers.title: Orthogonality of Defect Ideals for Jordan Homomorphisms
papers.abstract: Let $\varphi\colon A\to B$ be a Jordan homomorphism of associative algebras over a field $\mathbb{F}$ of characteristic different from $2$, with defect ideals $V_{\varphi}$ and $W_{\varphi}$. If $A=\operatorname{Alg}([[A,A],[A,A]])$, then $V_{\varphi}W_{\varphi}=W_{\varphi}V_{\varphi}=0$ and $V_{\varphi}\cap W_{\varphi}\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}(\operatorname{Alg}(\varphi(A)))$. Moreover, the induced map modulo $V_{\varphi}\cap W_{\varphi}$ is standard. The annihilator bound is sharp, even in finite dimension. As an application, when $A$ is unital and $A=K(A)$, every Jordan homomorphism defined on $A$ is splittable and standard. In this setting, the corresponding result of Brešar and Zelmanov holds without the surjectivity hypothesis.

papers.title: Alpern Lemma Independent of a Partition for Aperiodic Systems
papers.abstract: We prove that for every $(X,\mathcal{B},μ,T)$, an aperiodic, probability preserving system and $\mathcal{P}$ a finite measurable partition of $X$, there exists an Alpern Multitower whose base is independent of $\mathcal{P}$. This removes the ergodicity assumption in the original proof of the independent Alpern Lemma of \cite{MR3373823}. As a consequence, we remove ergodicity assumption from recent results on limit theorems in deterministic systems \cite{Kosloff_Volny_2022,kosloffVolnyStableCLT,MR4955410}.

papers.title: Matroid-Aware Spectral Certificates for Multiplicative Coverage Approximation
papers.abstract: We maximize the weight of edges covered by selected vertices, together with nonnegative individual rewards, under an arbitrary matroid constraint. The continuous coverage objective is quadratic and need not be concave. Our method searches projections onto a small set of directions and solves a concave subproblem for each projection center. A coverage-specific inequality converts the subproblem bounds into a multiplicative guarantee, while matroid rounding restores an integral solution. Let $A$ be the weighted adjacency matrix and $D$ the diagonal matrix of singleton values, restricted to positive-value elements after objective-preserving preprocessing. Set $\varrho=λ_{\max}(D^{-1/2}AD^{-1/2})$. For an integer budget $q\ge0$, let $τ_q$ be the smallest nonnegative threshold for which $A+τ_qD$ has at most $q$ negative eigenvalues on the span of differences of matroid bases. We obtain the factor $1-\varrhoτ_q/[2(\varrho+τ_q)]-\varepsilon$ in time $(2+q/\varepsilon)^{O(q+1)}N^{O(1)}$, where $N$ is the binary input length and a zero-over-zero loss is zero. The algorithm returns a rational upper bound on the integral optimum. A separate exact-algebraic construction produces polynomial-bit low-rank rational corrections with positive threshold slack; its proof isolates eigenvalues, keeps eigenspace bases unnormalized, and approximates scalar factors only at the final step. The numerical proposal prototype is not used to justify this complexity statement. Supplied certificates also yield robustness to locally bounded edge additions. These are threshold-dependent coverage guarantees, not a new general spectral-search principle or a universal approximation improvement.

papers.title: Covariance-Rank Rounding and a Sharp Integrality Gap for a Matroid Edge-Coverage Moment Lift
papers.abstract: Selecting vertices covers their incident edges, but a matroid can prevent selecting the combinations that cover the most weight. We study whether pair-selection information improves rounding from a semidefinite relaxation of this problem. A feasible point $(x,Y)$ records individual and paired selection values. Its relaxation objective is $U$, and the matrix $Y-xx^\top$ has rank $d$. We compare the feasible marginal vectors obtained by fixing one element as selected or excluded, then round only the best vector. For $d\ge1$, the resulting basis has value at least $(3/4+1/(4d))U$. The procedure is deterministic and polynomial-time for a supplied exact rational point and an independence oracle. Weighting the covariance spectrum by the objective gives a stronger version of the bound. To show the rank factor is sharp, we construct a rank-$2m$ rational linear matroid and $m$ disjoint four-cycles with integral optimum $3m+1$, relaxation optimum $4m$, and an optimal covariance matrix of rank $m$. Thus the relaxation has limiting reciprocal integrality gap $4/3$, despite its conditional constraints. One valid pair-exclusion inequality makes it exact on this family, as an explicit semidefinite certificate shows. The result concerns rounding and the strength of this relaxation; it does not supply a low-rank optimal point or a fixed universal approximation improvement.

papers.title: Another Brick in the Wall: A Computationally Assisted Proof of an Improved Upper Bound for Thrackles
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a thrackle, where a thrackle is a graph drawing in which each edge meets every other edge exactly once, either at a vertex or at a crossing. It is conjectured that, for all thrackles, the number of edges is less than or equal to the number of vertices. Fulek and Pach created a program to determine whether or not a graph can be a thrackle. Through a reconstruction and improvement of their algorithm, we computationally prove a key dumbbell to be non-thrackleable. Using this exclusion, we improve Xu's 8-face half-edge bound from five to four. Finally, using this stronger restriction with Xu's framework, together with separate arguments for graphs containing triangles and disconnected graphs, we improve the known upper bound toward this conjecture to $m\le1.385(n-1)$ for $n\ge4$.

papers.title: Mirror subspace diagonalization: a real-time quantum Krylov algorithm with near-optimal sampling cost
papers.abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41534-026-01384-yMirror subspace diagonalization: a real-time quantum Krylov algorithm with near-optimal sampling cost

papers.title: Large Deviations of Invariant Measures of Fractional Reaction-Diffusion Equations Driven by Multiplicative Noise on R^n
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish large deviations of invariant measures for fractional stochastic reaction-diffusion equations with polynomial reaction term driven by unbounded multiplicative noise on R^n. Under a dissipativity condition, we first prove the Freidlin-Wentzell large deviation principle of solution trajectories uniformly over all initial data in L^2(R^n). The key ingredient is a positive-time L^\infty-estimate for differences of controlled solutions which is independent of all initial data and hence yields uniform convergence of controlled stochastic solutions over the entire tphase space. Then using the uniform trajectory estimates, contraction and a second-moment estimate, we further prove the large deviations of invariant measures of the equation with a good quasipotential without introducing weighted spaces or establishing exponential tightness. The non-compactness of Sobolev embeddings in R^n is circumvented by uniform spatial tail-ends estimates. This is the first result on large deviations of invariant measures of the equation with multiplicative noise on unbounded domains.

papers.title: What remains when integrability fails? Mathematical structure in the K(m,m) compacton equations
papers.abstract: Peter Lax's 1968 discovery that certain nonlinear wave equations possess operator pairs (Lax pairs) opened the theory of completely integrable systems, yielding exact solutions, infinite conservation hierarchies, and perfectly elastic soliton collisions. When a nonlinear dispersive equation is provably non-integrable (admitting no Lax pair and only finitely many conservation laws), what mathematical structure governs its dynamics? The K(m,m) compacton equations, u_t + (u^m)_x + (u^m)_{xxx} = 0 for m >= 2, provide a testing ground: they support traveling waves with compact support, yet fail every known integrability test. We prove universal algebraic formulas determining the shape, width, and speed of every K(m,m) compacton. We develop a constraint-deficit mechanism explaining how the five independent conservation laws constrain emergent amplitudes and suppress the fundamental Fourier mode of the collision debris, while higher radiation modes remain unconstrained. The mechanism's conclusions rest on explicit hypotheses supported by numerical evidence. A phase-plane analysis reveals the compacton as a singular limit of smooth solitary waves through simultaneous regularity loss and support compactification. These results delineate intermediate territory between integrable order and generic nonlinear dynamics, organized by scaling universality and by the constraint deficit of a finite conservation structure.

papers.title: Modeling soliton-potential interactions for the 1-D cubic NLS via an invariant-preserving finite-difference method
papers.abstract: We consider the 1-D focusing cubic NLS with a smooth, spatially-dependent potential which decays rapidly as $x \rightarrow \pm \infty$. As is well known, under sufficient regularity conditions, solutions of the cubic NLS with such a spatially-dependent potential conserve both mass and energy. Additionally, in the absence of a potential, the 1-D focusing cubic NLS admits boosted soliton solutions. Furthermore, in the presence of a potential, the interaction of the potential with boosted soliton solutions to the free case is of active interest in the literature, particularly with respect to the dependence of this soliton-potential interaction on the velocity of the incident soliton. We adapt a finite-difference scheme to the setting of a smooth, rapidly-decaying spatially-dependent potential and show that this adaptation preserves the appropriate mass and energy invariants. Additionally, we use this algorithm to model soliton-potential interactions at a variety of incident soliton velocities.

papers.title: Fundamental Limits of Prescribed-Time Regulation: Gain Budgets, Accuracy Frontiers, and Arrival Costs
papers.abstract: Prescribed-time controllers drive the state to the origin at a time $T$ chosen in advance, with gains that grow without bound as $t$ approaches $T$. This paper shows the growth is a necessity and computes the exact price of avoiding it. The starting point is a simple estimate: any trajectory with $\|\dot z(t)\|\le L(t)\|z(t)\|$ satisfies $\|z(t)\|\ge\|z(0)\|e^{-\int_0^t L}$. From this: a gain profile $L$ supports exact prescribed-time convergence, over the unrestricted class of closed-loop vector fields admitting it, if and only if its integral over $[0,T)$ is infinite; so every design must either use an envelope of infinite integral or violate the linear growth bound at the origin, as finite-time and fixed-time designs do. Under a finite gain budget $\mathcal B=\int_0^T L$ the best worst-case contraction over the class is exactly $e^{-\mathcal B}$, a floor valid for every plant, and a finite-budget trajectory converges to a definite point away from the origin. A comparison lemma then carries the theory beyond linear growth: for envelopes $\|\dot z\|\le L(t)\,ω(\|z\|)$, first arrival at the origin requires budget at least $\int_0^{\|z_0\|}du/ω(u)$; arrival is impossible whenever this integral diverges, and when it is finite it is the exact threshold, attained inside the class. The classical settling expressions of finite-time control reappear as hitting-time floors, and the known fixed-time condition is the two-ended convergence of the same integral. For linear time-varying loops the results refine to logarithmic-norm budgets, corollaries of a known two-sided estimate, with the terminal error of gain freezing described exactly.

papers.title: Cyclic reflections and the flip equation for the graded Grothendieck-Teichmüller group
papers.abstract: Furusho, Hirose and Komiyama reformulated the pentagon equation using an involution called the flip, which led to a new characterisation of the graded Grothendieck-Teichmüller group $\mathsf{GRT}_1$. We show that the flip is a reflection in the cyclic structure of the operad of framed Drinfeld-Kohno Lie algebras, with the framings removed. Applying the reflection twice to the pentagon gives the two-cycle relation for every Drinfeld associator. This relation is precisely the condition for cyclic compatibility on the associativity morphism, giving a new proof that $\mathsf{GRT}_1$ acts by cyclic automorphisms of parenthesized ribbon chord diagrams.

papers.title: Limit Theorems for the Complete Feedback Card Guessing Game
papers.abstract: We study the optimal score $T_{n,m}$ in a complete feedback card guessing game. The deck has $n$ types and $m$ cards of each type. Its predictable compensator $S_{n,m}$ is the sum of the conditional success probabilities. We prove that Var$(S_{n,m})\leq C((\log\log n)^2+m/\log n)$, uniformly in $m$ for large $n$. This bound yields a central limit theorem for every sequence $m=m_n\geq1$ as $n\to\infty$. The score variance is asymptotic to its mean. We also give uniform Kolmogorov bounds using the conditional Bernoulli moments. For $m,n\to\infty$, the excess mean is asymptotic to $(\log n)\log\min\{m,\log n\}+(π/\sqrt2)\sqrt{m\log n}$. The two contributions balance at $m\asymp(\log n)(\log\log n)^2$. The variance proof uses reversed occupancy hitting times. Discrete hypergeometric tail estimates control their fluctuations in the large-deviation, Gaussian, and saturation regimes. For fixed $n$, we also show that the compensator has a Brownian-bridge functional limit as $m\to\infty$.

papers.title: Balancing cost and demand in a smart grid - a mean-field game analysis
papers.abstract: In a smart grid, consumers can also play the role of producers and sellers of energy. Therefore, the control of a smart grid over time becomes a dynamic game with a large number of small players and one or several large players. This is much more complicated than the control of an energy system with a single producer. The framework of mean-field games with common noise allows the transformation of such a complicated model into a control problem for a typical prosumer (producer and consumer in one) optimizing his behavior against a flow of other such prosumers. In our model, we introduce 2 decision variables for such a controller: one describing the amount of electric energy bought from the grid (or sold to it), and the second one describing the charging rate for our battery. The cost function is designed to satisfy two goals: satisfying the demand of the consumer (a single home) and minimizing the payment for energy. Players are allowed to sell/buy energy from the grid. Common noise is hidden in price volatility and sun irradiance, which influence all the players. We compute the optimal controls for our model and simulate solutions on real data. The novelty of our construction, compared to other works on smart grid control, lies in combining the minimization of the cost of energy and sustaining some level of demand satisfaction. We analyze the impact of battery usage on achieving a balance between these two criteria. We also take into account that the smart grid is only part of the energy market, which makes consumer strategies dependent on energy consumption outside the grid.

papers.title: $a$-Numbers, higher Cartier ranks and maximality of van der Geer-van der Vlugt curves
papers.abstract:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $C_R$ be the van der Geer-van der Vlugt curve $y^p-y=xR(x)$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, where $R(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{h}a_ix^{p^i}$ is an additive polynomial of degree $p^h$. We determine the image and the rank of every power of the Cartier operator $\Cart$ on $H^0(C_R,\Omg)$. For $1\le r\le h-1$ the image of $\Cart^r$ is spanned by an explicit set of monomial differentials that does not depend on $R$, and $ank(\Cart^r)=p^{h-r-1} inom{p+r}{r+2}$. The last iterate detects the linear coefficient: $ank(\Cart^h)=0$ if $a_0=0$ and $ank(\Cart^h)= inom{(p-1)/2+h}{h+1}$ if $a_0
eq0$, so the nilpotency index of $\Cart$ is $h$ or $h+1$. Hence, for $h\ge2$, the loci $a_0=0$ and $a_0
e0$ have the same $a$-number, which is the largest $a$-number of a one-point Artin-Schreier curve with pole order $p^h+1$, but they share no Ekedahl-Oort type. Over finite fields we deduce that a curve over $\F_{p^{2n}}$ that is geometrically isomorphic to $C_R$ can be $\F_{p^{2n}}$-maximal or $\F_{p^{2n}}$-minimal only if $n\ge h$, and only if $n\ge h+1$ when $a_0
eq0$. Explicit examples show that the second bound is attained for $(p,h)=(3,1)$, $(3,2)$ and $(5,2)$.

papers.title: Mathematical framework for simulation of non-perturbative cavity optomechanics with plate-like dielectrics
papers.abstract: Cavity optomechanical models typically treat a sensor either as a perturbative polarizable object in a pre-existing optical field, or solve the field at a fixed equilibrium and linearize in a fixed optical-mode basis. Neither self-consistently determines the spatially resolved cavity field, the optical force, the mechanical equilibrium, and the back-action when a finite-thickness dielectric plate intercepts the entire optical mode and restructures the intracavity field. In this companion paper to [1], we develop that treatment by extending the vacuum two-photon formalism to finite-thickness planar dielectrics, incorporating their Fresnel reflection, internal propagation, optical forces, and mechanical back-action directly into the field equations. We derive the carrier and sideband transfer functions needed to describe the coupled optical-mechanical system, including optomechanical cooling and the response to external perturbations. The result is a systematic starting point for calculating detector response and noise budgets for cavity experiments with intracavity dielectrics, including gravitational wave detectors deploying levitated sensors.

papers.title: Compactness of Cone Yang-Mills Connections
papers.abstract: We consider the cone Yang-Mills functional recently introduced by Tseng and Zhou. This functional generalizes the Yang-Mills functional by coupling it to a closed 2-form which can represent a geometric structure of interest, e.g. a symplectic form or Ricci form. While the perspective of dimensional reduction is not always possible, we show that a cone Yang-Mills field is always locally the dimensional reduction of a pure Yang-Mills field. We then prove a monotonicity formula and use the dimensional reduction framework to prove an $ε$-regularity theorem in two ways. Finally, we prove a compactness theorem for sequences of cone Yang-Mills connections with bounded action and $L^p$-bounded Higgs fields. Away from a singular set of codimension at least 4 and after suitable bundle identifications, the sequence subconverges in the $C^\infty_{\operatorname{loc}}$-topology.

papers.title: Time-Domain Observables for Resonant Scattering in Quantum Simulations of Lattice Gauge Theory
papers.abstract: Quantum computing may allow unprecedented access to nonequilibrium quantum dynamics, including problems of interest in particle physics, like the real-time development of scattering processes. Although fault-tolerant simulations at scale are still in the future, recent advancements toward early fault-tolerant simulations motivate building increasingly elaborate benchmark problems in order to assess state-of-the-art capabilities and test new algorithms and observables. In this work, we study glueball scattering on a line-of-plaquettes lattice in pure $SU(3)$ lattice gauge theory. We characterize scattering of the lowest-energy glueball states using classical exact diagonalization methods, identifying the continuum resonance structure using real-time simulations and approximate analytic methods, and we propose time-domain observables for extracting properties of the resonance from quantum simulations. We furthermore construct a toy model that shares the spectral features of the lattice gauge theory and demonstrate extraction of the observables. Feasibility on near-term hardware is demonstrated through simulation of a resonant collision of this toy model on Quantinuum System Model $\texttt{H2-2}$, with a 14-plaquette chain encoded in 28 qubits. The Trotterized circuit after optimization and compression requires $\sim 25n$ entangling gates for $n$ Trotter steps.

papers.title: Optimal Feature-Based Newsvendor Policies under Censored Demand
papers.abstract: We investigate a newsvendor problem where a decision-maker observes a $z$-dimensional vector of covariates, and wants to learn how much stock to order given a sample of size $n$ of censored demand data to minimize costs. Demand is censored when insufficient stock is available to meet it, and past stocking quantities are known. We propose a new model-agnostic loss function approach to estimate optimal order quantities using observational data, and characterize the optimal newsvendor policy as the policy that minimizes our proposed loss function. Our method requires only a single estimation step, can be scaled to datasets with hundreds of thousands of data points, and does not suffer from the same instabilities as inverse censoring probability weighting methods. We describe how this loss function can be implemented in linear empirical risk minimization, kernel weights optimization and deep neural network algorithms, and provide excess risk generalization bounds for their out-of-sample performance. Moreover, we show through numerical experiments that our method quickly converges to the optimal policy on synthetic data, and leads to improved performance on real world retail data.

papers.title: Large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials and trilinear sums over short intervals
papers.abstract: Recently, Matomäki, Pandey, Pliego, Teräväinen and Wang improved the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate of trilinear sums over short intervals of length $x^θ$, which naturally reduces to estimating mean values of products of three Dirichlet polynomials. Based on recent works of Guth and Maynard and Chen, Gupta and Li on new large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials, they improved the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate for $θ> \frac{3}{5}$. In this paper, we use their method to improve the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate for $\frac{1}{2} < θ< \frac{4}{7}$ and get new results for all $\frac{1}{2} < θ< 1$. Our result yields improvements on many problems, including the work of Li on primes in short intervals of length $x^{0.52}$.

papers.title: Functional Projection and Complexity Reduction
papers.abstract: Törnquist (arXiv:1310.3250) proved that if there exists a $\boldsymbolΣ^1_2$ maximal almost disjoint (MAD) family, then there exists a $\boldsymbolΠ^1_1$ MAD family. Since then, several other "complexity reduction" proofs have been found for other combinatorial objects, such as maximal independent families or ultrafilters. All of these proofs have relied on $\boldsymbolΠ^1_1$-uniformization, so they did not easily lift to higher projective levels. In this paper, we introduce a principle weaker than Uniformization which we call "Functional Projection", and show that this principle is sufficient for most complexity reduction proofs. On the other hand, we prove that in $L[U]$, the canonical inner model for a measurable cardinal, Functional Projection holds for $\boldsymbolΠ^1_2$ relations. As an immediate corollary, we obtain that in $L[U]$ there are $\boldsymbolΠ^1_2$ witnesses for many combinatorial families.

papers.title: Norm properties of quantum uniformity measures
papers.abstract: We prove that for $k=4$ the quantum uniformity measures are norms, whereas for every $k\geq5$ the triangle inequality fails. This gives a complete answer to an open question of Bu, Gu, and Jaffe. The $k=4$ case is proved using the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality for the quantum uniformity pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{Q^4}$ introduced here, together with the triangle inequality in a suitable finite-dimensional Bochner $L^8$ space. For $k\geq5$, we construct systems of linear equations over a finite field and derive a contradiction from the structure theory of norming linear systems.

papers.title: Distributed quantum phase sensing using an SU(1,1) Perelomov coherent state in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer network
papers.abstract: We present a theoretical study of distributed quantum sensing using a reconfigurable network of $N$ Mach--Zehnder interferometers to simultaneously estimate weighted linear combinations of relative phase shifts. The proposed scheme relies on injecting a Perelomov coherent state, generated from the SU(1,1) group representation, into one port of a passive quantum circuit while the remaining modes are initialized in the vacuum state, thereby establishing non-trivial quantum correlations among the sensors. Based on multi-parameter quantum estimation theory, our analysis shows that this entangled strategy outperforms the standard shot-noise limit and asymptotically achieves the Heisenberg limit. Furthermore, we highlight the crucial role of the first beam splitter's asymmetry; specifically, the optimal transmission coefficient that maximizes sensitivity corresponds to its maximum imbalance. Compared to a separable approach utilizing the same total average photon number, the entangled strategy yields a more efficient use of quantum resources, guaranteeing an accuracy gain between $1$ and $N$. This demonstrates that the entangled strategy is systematically superior to its separable counterpart. Ultimately, these results illustrate the potential of entangled distributed quantum sensor networks for high-precision measurements and provide clear guidelines for optimizing interferometric architectures in quantum metrology.

papers.title: Spectral Self-Concordant Barriers: A Proof of a Conjecture by Tunçel
papers.abstract: Let $Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a open, convex, and symmetric set and let $f:Q \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a $\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier function, that is also symmetric. We show the associated spectral function $F(X)= \mathcal{O}^2 (f \circ λ)(X)$ is a $\mathcal{O}^2\vartheta$-self-concordant function, where $\mathcal{O} = 8\max\{1+3\vartheta, 12\}$, on the domain of all $n \times n$ symmetric matrices $X$, with eigenvalues $λ(X) \in Q$. This generalizes the relationship between the standard logarithmic barriers $-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i$ and $-\log \det X$ and gives a solution to a conjecture by L.~Tunçel, 1995.

papers.title: Linear Laurent phenomenon algebras are of finite type
papers.abstract: Laurent phenomenon algebras generalise cluster algebras by allowing irreducible exchange polynomials in place of binomials. Lam and Pylyavskyy proved finite type for those arising from graphs and conjectured that the same holds for every Laurent phenomenon algebra admitting a linear seed. We prove this conjecture over an arbitrary unique factorisation domain. Our proof constructs a nonzero element of the upper algebra divisible by every cluster variable. Comparing noninitial cluster variables with the prime factors of this element in the initial Laurent ring bounds the number of cluster variable classes and yields a finite normalised mutation pattern.

papers.title: Model theory of quasitracial $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras and the absoluteness of monotone completeness
papers.abstract: We examine various applications of logic to $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras, particularly the monotone completeness conjecture. We develop a model theory for $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras equipped with a faithful normalized quasitrace. Using this language, we provide a separable coding which allows us to reduce the finite case of the monotone completeness conjecture to monotone sequential completeness of $\mathrm{II}_1$ $\mathrm{AW}^*$-factors. Combining an explicit recursive axiomatization with the completeness theorem for continuous logic, we show that this case of the conjecture, and Kaplansky's problem whether every $\mathrm{AW}^*$-factor of type $\mathrm{II}_1$ is a von Neumann algebra, are each equivalent in ZFC to a $Π^0_2$ sentence of arithmetic, so that their answers are the same in every $ω$-model of ZFC. We also consider real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras. Here the Baer-$*$-ring notion of an abelian projection must be distinguished from commutativity; following the real-operator-algebra terminology we call the former semi-abelian. Handelman's matrix theorem implies that a real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebra with no nonzero central semi-abelian projection has $\mathrm{AW}^*$ complexification. We answer a number of other open problems in real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras.

papers.title: Delta functions, a local coarea formula and marginal distributions
papers.abstract: We define multidimensional delta functions as generalized functions by pulling back the Dirac delta function, as well as products of such. We prove various formulas including a local version of the coarea formula and we use delta functions to compute marginal probability distributions on spheres.

papers.title: Plane Cremona maps preserving a Euclidean volume form
papers.abstract: We give a presentation by generators and relations of the group of birational transformations of the plane preserving a differential form with poles along a triple line. This group strictly contains the automorphism group of the affine plane.

papers.title: On the generators of separable unital C*-algebras
papers.abstract: Using the recent single-generation theorem for von Neumann $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors with separable predual, we prove the following results on the generators of a separable unital C*-algebra. Let $A$ be a separable unital C*-algebra, and suppose that $\partial \mathrm{T}(A)$ is nonempty, compact, and zero-dimensional. Then (1) If $A$ has strict comparison of positive elements by tracial states, then $A$ can be generated by two ordinary elements. (2) If $A$ has real rank zero and $A$ has strict comparison of projections by tracial states, then $A$ is singly generated. In this case, its single generators form a norm-dense $G_δ$ subset of $A$. (3) If $A$ has strict comparison of positive elements by tracial states and there is a unitary $u\in A$ such that for every $τ\in \partial \mathrm{T}(A)$, (a): the spectral distribution of $u$ with respect to $τ$ is atomless and has full support on $\mathbb T$, and (b): for every $a\in A$, $$\lim_{t \to 0}\sup_{p\in D_τ, 0<τ(p)\leq t} \| p\bigl(π_τ(a)-\mathbb E_{D_τ}(π_τ(a))\bigr)p\|=0, $$ where $M_τ=π_τ(A)''$, $D_τ=π_τ(u)''$, $\mathbb E_{D_τ}: M_τ\to D_τ$ is the trace-preserving conditional expectation, and $π_τ$ is the GNS representation associated to $τ$, then $A$ is singly generated. In particular, Conclusion (3) above implies that the reduced group C*-algebra $\mathrm{C}_r^*(\mathbb F_n)$ is singly generated for every $n\in\{2,3,\ldots,\infty\}$.

papers.title: Group gradings, graded identities and central polynomials of algebras with almost polynomial $δ$-growth
papers.abstract: The finite-dimensional $F$-algebras $D=F(e_{11}+e_{33})+Fe_{22}+Fe_{12}+Fe_{13}+Fe_{23} \subseteq UT_3$ and $D_0=Fe_{22}+Fe_{33}+Fe_{12}+Fe_{13}+Fe_{14}+Fe_{23}+Fe_{24}+Fe_{34} \subseteq UT_4$ occupy a distinguished position in the theory of central polynomials. Together with the infinite-dimensional Grassmann algebra, these algebras generate the only varieties of almost polynomial growth of proper central codimensions. We determine finite generating sets for their $T$-spaces of central polynomials and compute their central and proper central codimensions. We also prove that every group grading on $D_0$ is isomorphic to an elementary grading and determine the identities and codimensions associated with all its $\mathbb{Z}_2$-gradings.

papers.title: Purely non-free actions on Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: A group of conformal automorphisms of a Riemann surface is said to act purely non-free, or to produce a gpnf-action, if each of its finite-order elements has fixed points. It is known that every finite group admits a gpnf-action on a suitable closed Riemann surface of genus at least two. If $G$ is an infinite countable group, and $X$ is an infinite-type orientable surface, without planar ends and whose space of ends is self-similar, then we observe that there is a Riemann surface structure on $X$ admitting a gpnf-action by $G$. We obtain upper bounds for those finite groups producing a gpnf-action on a closed Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$. If $G$ is a finite group, then its purely non-free genus $σ^{pnf}_{hyp}(G)$ is the minimum genus of at least two of a closed Riemann surface admitting a gpnf-action by $G$. This parameter is already known for cyclic, abelian non-cyclic groups, ${\mathcal A}_{4}$, ${\mathcal A}_{5}$ and ${\mathfrak S}_{4}$. For general $G$, we provide the value of $σ^{pnf}_{hyp}(G)$, correcting a previous statement on this value. In particular, we observe that every genus is the purely non-free genus of some group. As an application, we describe the minimal purely non-free actions for the family of metacyclic groups $G^{0}_{s}(n)=\langle x,y: x^{n}=y^{2}=1, yxy=x^{s}\rangle,$ where $n \geq 3$ and $2 \leq s \leq n-1$ is such that $s^{2} \equiv 1 \mod(n)$.

papers.title: Overlap, Not Moments: Finite-Sample Theory for Bridge Sampling
papers.abstract: Bridge sampling estimates of marginal likelihoods are routinely reported with a delta-method Monte Carlo standard error (MCSE). Existing theory is asymptotic and cannot say whether a given run is long enough to trust the estimate or its MCSE. We give finite-sample answers. The optimal bridge estimator fits a logistic regression that separates posterior from proposal draws, and its accuracy is governed by their overlap, within a factor of two of the classification's Bayes error. Because the estimating function is a sum of bounded terms, no moment conditions are needed, and all bounds hold uniformly over targets, proposals and dimensions. A number of draws inversely proportional to the overlap suffices and is necessary in the worst case, paralleling the exponential-in-Kullback--Leibler requirement of importance sampling. A Berry--Esseen bound with an explicit constant holds at the optimal rate, and the MCSE is accurate once the effective overlap is large; it is estimated at no cost. For Markov chain draws, the required sample size grows in proportion to the sampler's relaxation time, unavoidably in the worst case. The estimated bridge, the fixed-point iteration and the fitted proposal matter only at second order, and we give free diagnostics for sampler failure and misestimated autocorrelation.

papers.title: Steiner Minimal Trees in the Gromov--Hausdorff Space and in Gromov--Hausdorff Clouds
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of Steiner minimal trees spanning a finite family of metric spaces in two cases of the Gromov--Hausdorff theory. In the compact Gromov--Hausdorff space $\mathcal{M}$, every finite family of nonempty compact metric spaces is spanned by a shortest Steiner minimal tree whose Steiner vertices are again nonempty compact metric spaces. In a fixed Gromov--Hausdorff cloud $\mathcal{C}$, every finite family of proper, isometrically cobounded spaces admits a finite-length Steiner minimal tree all of whose vertices remain in $\mathcal{C}$. The compact case uses compact replacement through distance profiles and the Hausdorff hyperspace, and the cloud case uses pointed ultralimits.

papers.title: Fresnel scattering for open waveguide networks
papers.abstract: This paper concerns the Helmholtz scattering problem for open waveguide networks, extending the analysis from [arXiv:2302.04353, arXiv:2310.05816, arXiv:2401.04674] to plane-wave incident data. We first reduce the problem to a Fredholm second-kind integral equation on an infinite interface. This produces an integral representation of the solution to the original scattering problem, which is then used to obtain detailed asymptotic estimates of the solution at infinity. To leading order and away from the waveguides, the scattered field is itself a plane wave. Its amplitude and phase shift exhibit a jump across a critical polar angle depending on the direction of the incident plane-wave. Our estimates also imply that the scattered field is outgoing in a weak sense, allowing us to establish a uniqueness result. We conclude by calculating the waveguide-mode contributions to the scattered field in a perturbative regime.

papers.title: A Controlled Null Result for Per-Gate Riemannian Optimization in VQE
papers.abstract: Parametrized gates in a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) live on a product of unitary groups, which makes Riemannian optimization a natural candidate for improving training. We test this candidate in the clean per-gate setting: each single-qubit gate is optimized directly on U (2) and compared with Adam on an unconstrained Euler-angle chart representing the same physical gate, initialized from the same unitaries and tuned with a separate learning-rate sweep. On a validated hydrogen-chain benchmark, we find no measurable practical advantage from the Riemannian machinery. The direct manifold optimizer and the Euler-coordinate baseline are interleaved in final error and success rate; the classical coordinate baseline is not slower in iterations on the successful cells; and the choices of Riemannian metric, retraction, and momentum vector transport do not change the conclusion. We also identify four failure modes that can manufacture an apparent positive result: a trivial product-state benchmark, a projected-matrix Adam baseline that discards most of its own step, a non-unitary inherited Cayley retraction that lets the reported energy pass below the variational minimum, and a learning-rate grid whose optimum sits at its boundary. Each failure mode produced a plausible multi-seed result in our own workflow before being caught. The practical output of this paper is therefore a controlled null result and a validation checklist for VQE optimizer comparisons.

papers.title: The rational homology of independence complexes of Kneser graphs on triples
papers.abstract: The independence complex of the Kneser graph $\KG(n,k)$ is the simplicial complex of pairwise intersecting families of $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$; equivalently, it is a Vietoris--Rips complex of the $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$ under the symmetric-difference metric. Feng and Wang asked whether, for $n=3$, its reduced homology is nontrivial only in dimensions $6$ and $9$, and conjectured the rank in dimension $9$. We answer the question affirmatively over the rationals and determine all the associated Betti numbers. For every $k\ge0$, the only nonzero reduced Betti numbers using rationals of $\Ind(\KG(3,k))$ are \[ β_6=\binom{k+5}{7}+29\binom{k+6}{7} \qquad\text{and}\qquad β_9=\binom{k+6}{6}. \] The proof uses an inductive decomposition based on a simplicial retraction and Barmak's star clusters, Dowker duality together with Jonsson's computation of the homology of complexes of graphs with bounded covering number, and a relative Mayer--Vietoris spectral sequence which reduces the problem to the six-element sets.

papers.title: Towards a Characterization of Matrix Monotonicity via Radial Convexity
papers.abstract: The theory of matrix monotone functions of finite degree depends subtly on the matrix size. Motivated by this phenomenon, we introduce radial convexity of metrics with respect to matrix orders on the cone of positive definite matrices. We establish radial convexity of several natural metrics with respect to the Loewner order and then focus on the Frobenius norm. Using the Daleckii-Krein formula, we relate radial convexity to the positivity of the Hadamard square of the corresponding Loewner matrix. This leads us to conjecture that radial convexity of order $n$ is equivalent to matrix monotonicity of degree $n$, and we prove this equivalence in degree $2$. We further provide evidence in higher dimensions, obtain a characterization in degree $3$, and discuss extensions of our results to arbitrary unitarily invariant norms.

papers.title: A Method for Exact Enforcement of Boundary Conditions on General Curved Triangular Domains: Algorithm and Application to Scientific Machine Learning
papers.abstract: We present a method for enforcing exactly Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin conditions on general triangular domains with arbitrarily curved boundaries. The algorithmic constructions developed here complements those in a previous work for general quadrilateral domains. Our method combines (i) the exact mapping between a general curved triangular domain and the standard triangle, (ii) TFC constrained expressions, and (iii) Barnhill transfinite interpolations, to provide explicit closed-form trial ansatze that mathematically satisfy the imposed boundary conditions exactly. Corner compatibility induced by the boundary conditions is pivotal, and enforcing exactly the imposed boundary conditions hinges on the exact enforcement of the induced compatibility constraints. The corner compatibility associated with the acute vertices of the standard triangle and the coupling between gradient components when the hypotenuse corresponds to a Neumann/Robin boundary pose particular challenges. Two strategies are critical to resolving these issues, by reformulating conditional corner constraints into equivalent unconditional forms and by introducing a separate TFC-style auxiliary edge construction together with an associated linear solve on the hypotenuse. We analyze the corner compatibility constraints and present formulations for the general form of functions that exactly satisfy the imposed Dirichlet, Neumann, or Robin conditions on curved triangular domains. The proposed method has been implemented using extreme learning machine type randomized neural networks for solving PDE problems. We present ample numerical experiments with linear/nonlinear PDE problems on a variety of domains with complex boundary geometries. Numerical results show that the current method has enforced the Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin conditions on curved domain boundaries to the machine precision.

papers.title: A characterization of central extensions relative to n-nilpotent objects
papers.abstract: We characterize the central extensions, in the sense of the categorical theory of central extensions of Janelidze and Kelly, relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of $n$-nilpotent objects of a semi-abelian and algebraically coherent category. An extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ turns out to be central precisely when the iterated Huq commutator $[A,[A,\dots,[A,K]\dots]]$, with $n$ occurrences of $A$, vanishes. For $n=2$ this condition reads $[A,[K,A]] = 0$, that is, $[K,A]$ is a central subobject of $A$. In the special case of groups this description was obtained by Everaert and the first author. The present proof is categorical, and applies in particular to Lie algebras, to crossed modules, to cocommutative Hopf algebras over a field, and to any category of interest.

papers.title: Hanslick's Musical Formalism as a Mathematical Structure - Examining meaning in Music through the Lens of Category Theory
papers.abstract: We investigate Eduard Hanslicks formalist aesthetics through the prism of Category Theory

papers.title: Beyond periodicity: Fourier methods for optimal control
papers.abstract: Fourier-based spectral methods provide compact global approximations, permit simple differentiation and integration, and achieve spectral convergence for smooth periodic functions. Their use in finite-horizon optimal control problems (OCPs) is nevertheless challenged by the generally nonperiodic state and control trajectories: endpoint mismatch induces artificial discontinuities and can destroy spectral convergence.
